description: Classification of the consent event. 'initial' = first consent for study participation; 're_consent' = repeat consent after protocol amendment; 'amendment' = consent to a specific protocol change; 'optional_procedure' = consent for an optional sub-study
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.8; 21 CFR Part 50; EU CTR 536/2014

description: Role of the staff member who obtained consent. 'PI' = Principal Investigator; 'sub_investigator' = Sub-Investigator; 'CRC' = Clinical Research Coordinator; 'delegate' = other delegated staff member listed on the delegation log.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.1; 21 CFR Part 312.62; FDA Delegation of Authority

description: Timestamp when this consent record was first created in the Silver Layer lakehouse. Supports ALCOA+ audit trail requirements and data lineage tracking.
reference: ALCOA+; 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) Section 8; GDPR Article 5(2)

business_glossary_term: Data Use After Withdrawal Permitted Flag
description: Indicates whether the subject explicitly permitted use of previously collected data after withdrawal of consent. Critical for GDPR right-to-erasure compliance and statistical analysis plan (the source system) decisions on data inclusion.
reference: GDPR Article 17; ICH E6(R2) Section 4.8.3; FDA Guidance on Informed Consent; HIPAA

description: Percentage of the eConsent workflow modules completed by the subject in Clinpal (0.00–100.00). Used to track partial completions and identify subjects who did not fully review all consent materials before signing.
reference: FDA Guidance on Use of Electronic Informed Consent (2016); Clinpal eConsent Platform; ICH E6(R2) Section 4.8

description: Legal basis under GDPR Article 9 for processing the subject's special category (health) data. 'explicit_consent' = subject provided explicit consent per Article 9(2)(a); 'vital_interests' = Article 9(2)(c); 'public_interest' = Article 9(2)(i) for
reference: GDPR Article 9; GDPR Article 6; EU CTR 536/2014; EMA Guidance on GDPR in Clinical Trials

description: Indicates whether a HIPAA Authorization for use and disclosure of Protected Health Information (PHI) was obtained from the subject, as required for U.S. clinical trials. May be combined with or separate from the ICF.
reference: HIPAA 45 CFR Part 164.508; 21 CFR Part 50; FDA Guidance on HIPAA and Clinical Research

business_glossary_term: Informed Consent Form (ICF) IRB/IEC Approval Date
description: Date on which the IRB or IEC approved the specific ICF version used for this consent event. Confirms that the consent was obtained using a currently approved document, a key GCP compliance check.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 3.1; 21 CFR Part 56; EU CTR 536/2014 Article 9

description: Indicates whether a Legally Authorized Representative (LAR) provided consent on behalf of the subject (e.g., for subjects who lack decision-making capacity, minors, or cognitively impaired individuals).
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.8.12; 21 CFR Part 50.3(l); EU CTR 536/2014 Article 31

description: Deadline by which the subject must complete re-consent to remain eligible for continued study participation. Populated when reconsent_required is True. Drives site monitoring alerts.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.8.2; 21 CFR Part 50; Oracle Siebel CTMS monitoring workflow

description: Indicates whether the subject is required to provide re-consent due to a protocol amendment, new safety information, or ICF version update. Triggers re-consent workflow in Clinpal.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.8.2; 21 CFR Part 50; FDA Guidance on Informed Consent Amendments

description: Reason that triggered the re-consent requirement. 'protocol_amendment' = protocol change affecting subject participation; 'safety_update' = new safety information impacting risk-benefit; 'icf_version_update' = new IRB-approved ICF version
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.8.2; 21 CFR Part 50; EU CTR 536/2014 Article 29

business_glossary_term: Biological Sample Use After Withdrawal Permitted Flag
description: Indicates whether the subject permitted continued use of previously collected biological samples (e.g., blood, tissue) after withdrawal of consent. Distinct from data_use_after_withdrawal as it governs physical biospecimen retention.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.8.3; GDPR Article 17; 21 CFR Part 50; EU Biobanking Regulations

description: Indicates whether the subject's questions and the investigator's responses were documented during the consent discussion, as required by GCP. Supports audit readiness and IRB inspection compliance.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.8.10; 21 CFR Part 50.25; OHRP Guidance

description: ISO 639-1/639-2 language code of the ICF translation provided to the subject (e.g., 'es' for Spanish, 'fr' for French, 'zh-CN' for Simplified Chinese). Null if the ICF was provided in the site's primary language.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.8.6; 21 CFR Part 50.25; ISO 639-1; EU CTR 536/2014

description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to this consent record in the Silver Layer lakehouse. Required for change tracking, audit trail completeness, and ALCOA+ compliance.
reference: ALCOA+; 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) Section 8; GDPR Article 5(2)

description: Date on which the subject formally withdrew consent to participate in the study. Populated only when consent_status is 'withdrawn'. Triggers subject discontinuation workflow.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.8.3; 21 CFR Part 50.25(a)(8); GDPR Article 7(3); EU CTR 536/2014

description: Primary reason for consent withdrawal as documented at the site. Used for subject disposition analysis and protocol feasibility reporting. Aligns with CDISC SDTM DS Domain disposition reason coding.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.8.3; CDISC SDTM DS Domain; 21 CFR Part 312.62

description: Full name of the impartial witness present during the informed consent process, where required. Captured when witness_required is True. Classified as confidential as it identifies a third-party individual in a clinical context.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.8.9; 21 CFR Part 50.27(b)

description: Indicates whether a witness was required for this consent event (e.g., for illiterate subjects, subjects with limited reading ability, or verbal consent scenarios per ICH E6(R2) Section 4.8.9).
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.8.9; 21 CFR Part 50.27(b)

description: Date on which the impartial witness signed the ICF, confirming they witnessed the consent process. Must match or follow the subject's consent_date.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.8.9; 21 CFR Part 50.27(b); ALCOA+

description: Unique surrogate identifier for each eConsent workflow session initiated in Clinpal for a trial subject. Primary key for this data product.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP

description: Reference to the specific IRB/IEC-approved Informed Consent Form (ICF) version presented to the subject during this session. Ensures the correct, current consent document was used.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.8; 21 CFR Part 50; EU CTR 536/2014

description: Reference to the clinical trial site at which the subject is enrolled and where this consent session is associated. Supports site-level compliance monitoring.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; Oracle Siebel CTMS

description: Reference to the clinical study (protocol) for which this eConsent session was conducted. Enables study-level consent compliance reporting.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 312

description: Foreign key linking to document.tmf_document. Business justification: Econsent session audit trails and e-signature records are TMF-filed under 21 CFR Part 11 and ICH E6(R2). Regulatory inspectors review econsent session records against TMF filings.
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Reference to the trial subject (participant) for whom this eConsent session was initiated. Links to the subject master record.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 50; GDPR Article 7

description: Result of the capacity assessment performed for the subject. 'capable' indicates the subject has decision-making capacity; 'not-capable' indicates a legally authorized representative is required; 'not-assessed' indicates no assessment was conducted
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.8; 21 CFR Part 50.20; OHRP Guidance; EU CTR 536/2014 Article 29

description: Indicates whether a formal capacity assessment was performed for the subject prior to or during this consent session (True = performed; False = not performed). Required for vulnerable populations and subjects with potential cognitive impairment.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.8; 21 CFR Part 50.20; EU CTR 536/2014 Article 29; OHRP Guidance

description: The native session identifier assigned by the Clinpal eConsent platform for this workflow session. Used for cross-system traceability and reconciliation with the source system of record.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; Clinpal eConsent Platform

description: The teleconference or video communication platform used for remote consent sessions (e.g., Zoom, Microsoft Teams, WebEx). Applicable only when session_modality is 'remote-video' or 'remote-phone'.
reference: FDA Remote Consent Guidance (2020); ICH E6(R2)

description: The sequential attempt number for the comprehension check within this session. Subjects may be permitted multiple attempts after remediation. Tracks how many times the subject attempted the comprehension assessment.
reference: FDA Guidance on Informed Consent (2016); ICH E6(R2) Section 4.8; Clinpal eConsent Platform

description: Version identifier of the comprehension check question set administered to the subject during this session. Ensures traceability to the specific validated question set used, as question sets may be updated with ICF amendments.
reference: FDA Guidance on Informed Consent (2016); ICH E6(R2) Section 4.8; Clinpal eConsent Platform

description: Indicates whether the subject passed the overall comprehension check for this session (True = passed; False = failed). Determined by comparing the score against the minimum passing threshold defined in the ICF version.
reference: FDA Guidance on Informed Consent (2016); ICH E6(R2) Section 4.8; Clinpal eConsent Platform

description: Number of comprehension check questions answered correctly by the subject in this session. Used to compute the overall comprehension score and determine pass/fail outcome.
reference: FDA Guidance on Informed Consent (2016); ICH E6(R2) Section 4.8

description: Total number of comprehension check questions administered to the subject in this session. Used to calculate the comprehension score and assess understanding of the consent content.
reference: FDA Guidance on Informed Consent (2016); ICH E6(R2) Section 4.8

description: Indicates whether the subject (or legally authorized representative) granted informed consent at the conclusion of this session (True = consent granted; False = consent not granted or declined). The definitive consent outcome flag for this session.
reference: 21 CFR Part 50; ICH E6(R2) Section 4.8; GDPR Article 7; HIPAA 45 CFR 164.508

description: The role of the individual who provided consent during this session. 'subject' indicates the participant themselves; 'legally-authorized-representative' indicates a proxy consenter; 'parent' or 'guardian' applies to pediatric studies.
reference: 21 CFR Part 50.25; ICH E6(R2) Section 4.8; EU CTR 536/2014 Article 29

description: Date and time (with timezone offset) when this eConsent session record was first created in the data platform. Supports ALCOA+ (Attributable, Contemporaneous) audit trail requirements.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+; GDPR Article 5(2); ICH E6(R2)

description: Operating system and version of the device used during the eConsent session (e.g., iOS 16.4, Android 13, Windows 11). Supports technical audit trail and system validation requirements under 21 CFR Part 11.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; FDA Remote Consent Guidance (2020)

description: Category of device used by the subject to access and complete the eConsent session. Supports technical audit trail requirements and device compatibility analysis.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; FDA Remote Consent Guidance (2020)

description: Indicates whether an electronic signature was successfully captured from the subject (or legally authorized representative) during this session (True = captured; False = not captured).
reference: 21 CFR Part 11 Section 11.50; ICH E6(R2) Section 4.8; EU CTR 536/2014

description: Date and time (with timezone offset) when the subject's electronic signature was captured in Clinpal. Critical for ALCOA+ (Contemporaneous) compliance and 21 CFR Part 11 audit trail. Null if no signature was captured.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11 Section 11.50; ALCOA+ (Contemporaneous); ICH E6(R2) Section 4.8

description: Indicates whether a language interpreter was used during the consent session (True = interpreter used; False = no interpreter). Relevant for non-English-speaking subjects and required for GCP documentation of consent comprehension.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.8; 21 CFR Part 50.25; FDA Guidance on Informed Consent (2016)

description: IP address of the device used by the subject during the eConsent session. Required for 21 CFR Part 11 electronic records audit trail and GDPR accountability. May be considered PII in certain jurisdictions.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11 Section 11.10; GDPR Article 4; HIPAA Security Rule

business_glossary_term: Institutional Review Board (IRB) / Independent Ethics Committee (IEC) Approval Reference
description: The IRB or IEC approval number or reference associated with the ICF version used in this session. Confirms the consent document presented was approved by the appropriate ethics body at the time of the session.
reference: 21 CFR Part 56; ICH E6(R2) Section 3.1; EU CTR 536/2014; OHRP 45 CFR Part 46

description: Indicates whether this session was initiated as a re-consent event (True) rather than an initial consent (False). Re-consent is triggered by protocol amendments, new safety information, or ICF version updates requiring subjects to re-affirm consent.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.8.2; 21 CFR Part 50.25; EU CTR 536/2014 Article 28

description: Indicates whether remediation (additional educational content or re-review of ICF sections) was provided to the subject following a failed comprehension check attempt (True = remediation was provided; False = not provided).
reference: FDA Guidance on Informed Consent (2016); ICH E6(R2) Section 4.8

description: Number of remediation steps (re-review sections or educational modules) completed by the subject following a failed comprehension check. Null if no remediation was provided.
reference: FDA Guidance on Informed Consent (2016); ICH E6(R2) Section 4.8; Clinpal eConsent Platform

description: The number of ICF review steps (content sections) the subject completed during this session. Compared against review_steps_total to assess session progress and identify drop-off points.
reference: Clinpal eConsent Platform; ICH E6(R2) Section 4.8; 21 CFR Part 11

description: The total number of review steps (content sections or pages) defined in the ICF version presented during this session. Used to calculate completion percentage and identify where subjects abandoned the session.
reference: Clinpal eConsent Platform; ICH E6(R2) Section 4.8

description: Date and time (with timezone offset) when the eConsent session concluded, regardless of outcome (completed, abandoned, timed-out, or declined). Null if the session is still in-progress.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+ (Contemporaneous); ICH E6(R2)

description: IETF BCP 47 language tag representing the language in which the eConsent session was conducted (e.g., 'en', 'es', 'fr-CA'). Ensures the subject received consent information in their preferred language, as required by GCP and GDPR.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.8; 21 CFR Part 50.25(b); GDPR Article 7; IETF BCP 47

description: The mode by which the consent session was conducted. 'in-person' indicates the subject and site staff were physically co-located; 'remote-video' indicates a teleconference/video call; 'remote-phone' indicates a telephone-only session; 'hybrid' indicates a
reference: FDA Remote Consent Guidance (2020); ICH E6(R2) Section 4.8; EU CTR 536/2014

description: Date and time (with timezone offset) when the eConsent session was initiated by the subject or site staff in Clinpal. Serves as the principal business event timestamp for this transaction.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+ (Contemporaneous); ICH E6(R2)

description: Current lifecycle state of the eConsent workflow session. 'in-progress' indicates an active session; 'completed' indicates the subject finished all steps; 'abandoned' indicates the subject exited without completing; 'timed-out' indicates the session
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; FDA Remote Consent Guidance (2020); ICH E6(R2)

description: The method used to authenticate the subject's identity at the start of the eConsent session. Supports 21 CFR Part 11 identity verification requirements for electronic signatures.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11 Section 11.100; ICH E6(R2) Section 4.8; GDPR Article 7

description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code representing the country where the subject was physically located at the time of the eConsent session. Relevant for decentralized trials and cross-border GDPR/HIPAA compliance determination.
reference: GDPR Article 3; HIPAA; ISO 3166-1; FDA Remote Consent Guidance (2020)

description: Free-text description of any technical issue encountered during the session (e.g., 'Video connection dropped at step 3', 'Signature pad unresponsive'). Null if no technical issue was encountered. Supports deviation investigation and CAPA processes.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2); MasterControl CAPA

description: Indicates whether any technical issue (connectivity failure, platform error, device malfunction, signature capture failure) was encountered during the session (True = issue encountered; False = no issues).
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; FDA Remote Consent Guidance (2020); Clinpal eConsent Platform

description: Date and time (with timezone offset) when this eConsent session record was last modified in the data platform. Supports change tracking and audit trail completeness under 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+; GDPR Article 5(2); ICH E6(R2)

description: Date and time (with timezone offset) when the site staff witness (PI or CRC) applied their electronic countersignature to the consent record. Required for GCP-compliant consent documentation. Null if witness signature was not captured in this session.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11 Section 11.50; ICH E6(R2) Section 4.8; 21 CFR Part 50

description: Unique surrogate identifier for the ICF amendment record in the Databricks Silver Layer. Primary key for this entity.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Good Clinical Practice; 21 CFR Part 50; EU CTR 536/2014

description: The workflow identifier assigned by the Clinpal eConsent system for the re-consent or new consent workflow triggered by this amendment. Enables traceability between the amendment record and the eConsent execution.
reference: Clinpal eConsent Platform; FDA Guidance on Use of Electronic Informed Consent; 21 CFR Part 11

description: Foreign key linking to study.country. Business justification: ICF amendments have country-specific applicability and require country-level regulatory submission and approval. The existing country_code plain attribute is a denormalization of study.country.
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Foreign key linking to compliance.ethics_approval. Business justification: GCP requires that amended ICFs are only implemented after ethics committee approval.
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Foreign key linking to compliance.ethics_submission. Business justification: An ICF amendment is formally submitted to the ethics committee via an ethics_submission.
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

business_glossary_term: Resulting Informed Consent Form (ICF) Version ID
description: Reference to the new ICF version produced as a result of this amendment. Null until the amended ICF version is formally approved and issued.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.8; Veeva Vault eTMF document versioning

description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.ind_application. Business justification: IB safety updates with new risk information directly trigger ICF amendments per ICH E6 GCP.
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Foreign key linking to study.protocol. Business justification: ICF amendments are directly triggered by protocol amendments and must reference the governing protocol version.
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Foreign key linking to document.regulatory_binder. Business justification: ICF amendments requiring regulatory submission (regulatory_submission_required flag) are filed in regulatory binders for agency review.
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Foreign key linking to study.study_protocol_amendment. Business justification: Protocol amendments directly drive ICF amendments — when a study_protocol_amendment is approved, corresponding ICF amendments must be issued.
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.submission. Business justification: ICF amendments with 'regulatory_submission_required=true' must be filed as part of a regulatory submission.
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Reference to the subsequent amendment that supersedes this one, if applicable. Null for the current active amendment. Enables full amendment lineage chain reconstruction for regulatory inspection.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.8; Veeva Vault eTMF; TMF Reference Model

description: Foreign key linking to safety.safety_communication. Business justification: Safety-related ICF amendments are directly triggered by safety communications (e.g., SUSAR letters, urgent safety measures).
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Foreign key linking to document.tmf_document. Business justification: ICF amendments are essential TMF documents (DIA TMF Reference Model). Regulatory inspectors verify amendments against TMF filings.
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Defines which subject population is required to undergo re-consent as a result of this amendment. Drives the re-consent workflow in Clinpal and determines the scope of CRA site monitoring activities.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.8.2; FDA Guidance on Informed Consent; OHRP; GDPR Article 7

description: The principal real-world date on which the amendment was formally initiated or authored. Serves as the primary business event date for the amendment lifecycle.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.8; ALCOA+ principles; 21 CFR Part 11

description: Externally-known sequential identifier for the amendment (e.g., AM-001, AM-002). Used in regulatory submissions, IRB/IEC correspondence, and TMF filing to uniquely reference the amendment within the study.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.8; FDA Guidance on Informed Consent; Veeva Vault eTMF

description: Current lifecycle state of the ICF amendment. Tracks progression from initial drafting through IRB/IEC submission, approval or rejection, and eventual supersession by a subsequent amendment.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 3.1; 21 CFR Part 56; EU CTR 536/2014 Article 15

description: Classification of the nature of change driving the amendment. Safety updates require expedited IRB/IEC review; protocol changes may require full board review; administrative corrections may qualify for expedited review.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.8.2; FDA 21 CFR Part 50.25; OHRP Guidance on Amendments

description: Indicates whether a subject capacity or competency assessment is required before re-consent can be obtained under this amendment. Relevant for vulnerable populations, pediatric studies, or subjects with cognitive impairment.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.8.9; 21 CFR Part 50.55; EU CTR 536/2014 Article 31; OHRP

description: Detailed narrative describing the nature and rationale of the changes introduced by this amendment. Captures what was changed, why it was changed, and the impact on subject safety or study conduct.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.8; FDA Guidance on Informed Consent; OHRP

description: Timestamp when this ICF amendment record was first created in the Databricks Silver Layer. Supports ALCOA+ audit trail requirements and data lineage tracking per 21 CFR Part 11.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+ principles; ICH E6(R2) Section 8

description: Risk classification assigned to the amendment indicating the potential for protocol deviations if re-consent is not completed within the required timeframe. Informs monitoring prioritization in the source system
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.20; FDA Guidance on Oversight of Clinical Investigations; MasterControl CAPA

description: Indicates whether the amended ICF will be deployed via the Clinpal eConsent platform. When True, triggers the eConsent build and validation workflow in Clinpal for the resulting ICF version.
reference: FDA Guidance on Use of Electronic Informed Consent; ICH E6(R2); 21 CFR Part 11; Clinpal eConsent

business_glossary_term: General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) Applicable Flag
description: Indicates whether GDPR data privacy provisions apply to this amendment, typically for studies enrolling subjects in EU/EEA countries. When True, the amended ICF must include GDPR-compliant data processing disclosures.
reference: GDPR Articles 6, 7, 9, 13, 14; EU CTR 536/2014; EMA

business_glossary_term: Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) Applicable Flag
description: Indicates whether HIPAA authorization provisions apply to this amendment, typically for studies enrolling subjects at U.S. sites. When True, the amended ICF must include a HIPAA-compliant authorization section.
reference: HIPAA 45 CFR Parts 160 and 164; FDA 21 CFR Part 50; OHRP

description: The date from which the amended ICF version becomes effective for use at clinical sites. Sites must not use the amended ICF prior to this date. Typically set to or after the IRB/IEC approval date.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.8; 21 CFR Part 50; EU CTR 536/2014

description: ISO 639-1 language code (optionally with ISO 3166-1 country subtag) of the amended ICF document (e.g., en-US, fr-FR, de-DE). Multi-language studies require separate amendment tracking per language version.
reference: ISO 639-1; ICH E6(R2) Section 4.8.6; GDPR Article 7; FDA Guidance on Informed Consent

business_glossary_term: Legally Authorized Representative (LAR) Consent Applicable Flag
description: Indicates whether consent from a Legally Authorized Representative (LAR) is applicable for this amendment, typically for subjects who lack decision-making capacity. Triggers LAR-specific consent workflow in Clinpal.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.8.9; 21 CFR Part 50.55; EU CTR 536/2014 Article 31; OHRP

description: Free-text field for additional operational notes, internal comments, or contextual information related to the amendment that does not fit into structured fields. Not intended for regulatory submission content.
reference: ICH E6(R2); ALCOA+ principles

description: The date by which all affected subjects must complete re-consent. Null when reconsent_required is False. Used to monitor site compliance and escalate overdue re-consent activities.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.8; FDA Guidance on Informed Consent; OHRP

description: Indicates whether currently enrolled subjects are obligated to provide re-consent under this amendment. True triggers re-consent workflow initiation in Clinpal and site notification via the source system
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.8.2; 21 CFR Part 50.25; OHRP Guidance; GDPR Article 7

description: Indicates whether this amendment must be submitted to a health authority (e.g., FDA, EMA) as part of an IND, CTA, or equivalent regulatory filing. True triggers a regulatory submission workflow in Veeva Vault.
reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 312.30; EMA EU CTR 536/2014; ICH E6(R2) Section 5.8

description: Free-text description of the reason provided by the IRB or IEC for rejecting or deferring the amendment. Populated only when irb_iec_decision is rejected or deferred. Required for CAPA tracking in MasterControl.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 3.1; 21 CFR Part 56.109; MasterControl CAPA

description: The regulatory authority, ethics committee, or organizational body that mandated or triggered this amendment. Supports regulatory inspection readiness by documenting the source of the amendment requirement.
reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 56; EMA EU CTR 536/2014; ICH E6(R2); MHRA; PMDA; TGA; Health Canada

description: Name or identifier of the Principal Investigator (PI) or medical monitor who reviewed and approved the amendment content prior to IRB/IEC submission. Supports GCP audit trail requirements.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.8; 21 CFR Part 312; ALCOA+ principles

description: Indicates whether this amendment was triggered by a safety finding, SUSAR, SAE signal, or DSMB/DMC recommendation. Safety-related amendments require expedited IRB/IEC review and may trigger immediate site notification.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.8.2; ICH E2A; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA GVP Module VI

description: Defines whether this amendment applies to all clinical sites globally, a specific subset of sites, or only sites within a particular country. Drives site notification and monitoring workflows in the source system
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.8; Oracle Siebel CTMS; FDA 21 CFR Part 50

description: Date on which the pharmaceutical or biotech sponsor formally approved the amendment content prior to IRB/IEC submission. Required for sponsor oversight documentation in the TMF.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.8; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; Veeva Vault eTMF

description: Timestamp when this ICF amendment record was last modified in the Databricks Silver Layer. Supports change tracking, audit trail completeness, and ALCOA+ contemporaneous documentation requirements.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+ principles; ICH E6(R2) Section 8

description: Unique surrogate identifier for each Informed Consent Form (ICF) version record in the consent master catalog. Primary key for this data product.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Good Clinical Practice; 21 CFR Part 50; EU CTR 536/2014

description: Foreign key linking to document.workflow. Business justification: ICF versions require sponsor and IRB approval workflows tracked in document management systems like Veeva Vault.
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.clinical_trial_authorization. Business justification: EU CTR 536/2014 requires ICF versions to be authorized under a specific CTA.
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Foreign key linking to compliance.compliance_sop. Business justification: ICF versions are authored from sponsor-approved document templates. Regulatory inspectors verify that the correct, current-version template was used to create each ICF.
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Foreign key linking to study.country. Business justification: Multi-country trials require country-specific ICF version approvals. Regulatory authorities in each country must approve the local-language ICF before subjects can be consented.
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.ind_application. Business justification: US IND annual reports must enumerate all ICF versions in use during the reporting period.
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

business_glossary_term: Parent Informed Consent Form (ICF) Version ID

description: Foreign key linking to laboratory.bioanalytical_assay. Business justification: SDTM PC domain mapping rules for PK concentration variables are assay-specific (analyte name, units, LLOQ derivation).
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Target SDTM variable specification this mapping produces (replaces free-text variable definition).

Foreign key linking to compliance.sop. Business justification: SDTM mapping activities are governed by SOPs (e.g., SOP for SDTM mapping, define.xml authoring). Regulatory submissions require SOP traceability for mapping decisions.
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Foreign key linking to study.endpoint. Business justification: SDTM mappings for endpoint variables must be traceable to the endpoint definition for submission package completeness review.
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Reference to the parent SDTM dataset specification record that owns this mapping rule. Establishes the header/detail relationship between the dataset-level specification and this individual variable mapping line.
reference: CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide v3.4

description: Foreign key linking to study.protocol. Business justification: SDTM mapping specifications are authored against a specific protocol version. Protocol amendments that change endpoints or visit schedules require mapping spec updates; direct protocol_id
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Foreign key linking to laboratory.reference_range. Business justification: SDTM LB domain mapping rules for normal range variables (LBORNRLO, LBORNRHI, LBNRIND) must reference the applicable reference range definition.
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Foreign key linking to biostatistics.the source system. Business justification: SDTM mapping specifications are governed by the the source system, which defines required SDTM domains, variables, and submission versions.
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Foreign key linking to datamanagement.ecrf_field. Business justification: sdtm_mapping defines transformation rules from raw EDC eCRF fields to SDTM variables. source_field_name and source_field_label are denormalized references to the source eCRF field.
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Foreign key linking to datamanagement.ecrf_form. Business justification: sdtm_mapping defines transformation rules from raw EDC eCRF fields to SDTM variables. source_form_name is a denormalized reference to the source eCRF form.
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Reference to the clinical study for which this SDTM mapping rule is defined. Enables study-scoped filtering and traceability of all mapping specifications back to the originating protocol.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide

description: Foreign key linking to study.study_protocol_amendment. Business justification: Protocol amendments that change data collection requirements trigger SDTM mapping specification updates.
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Date and time when this mapping rule was formally approved and promoted to 'approved' status by the authorized reviewer. Represents the principal business event timestamp for this mapping lifecycle transition.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+

description: Free-text justification for the most recent change to this mapping rule (e.g., 'Protocol Amendment 3 — new AE severity scale', 'Corrected derivation logic per QC review'). Required when mapping_status transitions or derivation_algorithm is modified.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+; FDA Study Data Technical Conformance Guide

description: Medical coding dictionary used for this mapping when derivation_type is 'coded'. MedDRA (Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities) for adverse events and medical history; WHO-DD (WHO Drug Dictionary) for concomitant medications; CTCAE (Common
reference: MedDRA; WHO-DD; CTCAE; ICH E2A; FDA Adverse Event Reporting

description: Version of the medical coding dictionary applied for this mapping (e.g., MedDRA v26.1, WHO-DD March 2023). Ensures reproducibility of coded terms across transformation runs and supports regulatory submission traceability.
reference: MedDRA; WHO-DD; ICH E2A; FDA Study Data Technical Conformance Guide

business_glossary_term: CDISC Controlled Terminology Code List Name
description: Name of the CDISC Controlled Terminology code list applied to this SDTM variable (e.g., 'AESEV', 'NCOMPLT', 'SEX', 'RACE'). Null if no controlled terminology applies. Governs permissible values for the target variable in regulatory submissions.
reference: CDISC Controlled Terminology; CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide; FDA Study Data Technical Conformance Guide

description: Date and time when this SDTM mapping rule record was first created in the system. Supports ALCOA+ audit trail requirements and 21 CFR Part 11 electronic records compliance. Immutable after initial record creation.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+

description: Version of the CDISC Controlled Terminology package applied for this mapping (e.g., '2023-09-29'). Ensures reproducibility of coded values across transformation runs and regulatory submissions. Critical for FDA/EMA submission compliance.
reference: CDISC Controlled Terminology; FDA Study Data Technical Conformance Guide; EMA Data Standards

description: Supplementary comment text to be included in the CDISC Define-XML v2.1 submission package for this variable. Provides additional context for FDA/EMA reviewers about the derivation logic, data source, or special handling.
reference: CDISC Define-XML v2.1; FDA Study Data Technical Conformance Guide

description: Origin attribute value for this variable as it will appear in the CDISC Define-XML v2.1 submission metadata. Indicates the source of the data: 'CRF' (collected on eCRF), 'Derived' (algorithmically derived), 'Assigned' (assigned by sponsor/CRO), 'Protocol'
reference: CDISC Define-XML v2.1; FDA Study Data Technical Conformance Guide

description: Full specification of the transformation logic or derivation rule applied to produce the target SDTM variable value from the source field(s). Includes SAS code snippets, conditional logic, date calculations, concatenation rules, and multi-source merge
reference: CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide; ALCOA+; 21 CFR Part 11; SAS Drug Development

description: Classification of the mapping derivation method: 'direct' (verbatim copy from source), 'derived' (computed from one or more source fields), 'assigned' (constant or protocol-defined value), 'predecessor' (derived from a previously mapped SDTM variable)
reference: CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide v3.4; FDA Study Data Technical Conformance Guide

description: Date after which this version of the mapping rule is no longer active and has been superseded or deprecated. Null for currently active mapping rules. Supports temporal versioning of mapping specifications across protocol amendments.
reference: CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide; ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+

description: Date from which this version of the mapping rule is effective and applicable to SDTM transformation runs. Supports version-controlled mapping specifications where different versions apply to different data collection periods or protocol amendments.
reference: CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide; ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+

description: Indicates whether this SDTM variable mapping requires data from more than one source field or form (True) or derives from a single source field (False). When True, the derivation_algorithm field documents all contributing source fields and the combination
reference: CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide; ALCOA+

description: Indicates whether the predecessor variable dependency documented in predecessor_variable is a hard requirement (True) that must be resolved before this mapping executes, or an informational dependency (False).
reference: CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide; SAS Drug Development

description: Indicates whether the target SDTM variable contains sensitive subject data requiring special handling under GDPR, HIPAA, or sponsor data privacy agreements (True). Examples include subject identifiers, dates of birth, and geographic data.
reference: GDPR Article 4; HIPAA; 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2)

description: Date and time when this SDTM mapping rule record was most recently updated. Updated on every change to the mapping rule, derivation logic, or status. Supports change tracking and ALCOA+ audit trail requirements.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+

description: Externally-known, human-readable unique code identifying this mapping rule within the study's SDTM mapping specification document. Follows the pattern MAP-{DOMAIN}-{VARIABLE}-{SEQUENCE}. Used in Data Management Plans (DMP) and CDISC submission packages.
reference: CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide; FDA Study Data Technical Conformance Guide

description: Current lifecycle state of this SDTM mapping rule. Controls which version is active for production CDISC transformation runs. 'approved' rules are eligible for DBL and regulatory submission.
reference: CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide; ICH E6(R2); 21 CFR Part 11

description: Version number of this mapping rule in major.minor format (e.g., 1.0, 2.3). Incremented when the transformation logic, source field, or controlled terminology mapping changes.
reference: CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide; 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+

description: Free-text field for additional programmer or reviewer notes about this mapping rule, including special handling instructions, known data quality issues, sponsor-specific requirements, or cross-references to related mapping rules.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+

description: Name of the SDTM variable (within the same or a different domain) that must be derived before this mapping can be executed. Documents derivation dependencies for sequencing transformation programs. Format: '{DOMAIN}.{VARIABLE}' (e.g., 'AE.AEDECOD').
reference: CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide; SAS Drug Development

description: Name or employee identifier of the Data Management or Biostatistics reviewer who reviewed and approved this mapping rule. Supports dual-review traceability and ALCOA+ compliance for the SDTM mapping specification document.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+; 21 CFR Part 11

description: Two-letter CDISC SDTM domain code identifying the target dataset domain (e.g., DM, AE, LB, VS, CM, EX, MH, DS, SV, TU). Determines the SDTM class and required/expected variable set for this mapping.
reference: CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide v3.4; CDISC Controlled Terminology

description: Version of the CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide that governs this mapping rule (e.g., 'SDTMIG v3.4', 'SDTMIG-AP v1.0'). Ensures regulatory submission compliance with the correct CDISC standard version as required by FDA and EMA data submission guidelines.
reference: CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide; FDA Study Data Technical Conformance Guide; EMA Data Standards

description: CDISC core designation indicating whether the target SDTM variable is Required (Req), Expected (Exp), or Permissible (Perm) for the domain. Required variables must be populated; Expected variables should be populated when data is collected; Permissible
reference: CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide v3.4; FDA Study Data Technical Conformance Guide

description: Human-readable descriptive label for the target SDTM variable as defined in the CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide (e.g., 'Dictionary-Derived Term', 'Numeric Result/Finding in Standard Units').
reference: CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide v3.4; CDISC Define-XML v2.1

description: Name of the target CDISC SDTM variable within the specified domain (e.g., AEDECOD, LBSTRESN, VSORRES). Must conform to CDISC SDTM naming conventions: uppercase, 2–8 characters, domain prefix for most variables.
reference: CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide v3.4; FDA Study Data Technical Conformance Guide

description: CDISC-defined role of the target SDTM variable within its domain class (Identifier, Topic, Qualifier, Timing, Rule). Determines how the variable functions within the SDTM dataset structure and governs its position and usage in regulatory submissions.
reference: CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide v3.4

description: CDISC-defined data type of the target SDTM variable. 'Char' for character/text variables and 'Num' for numeric variables, as specified in the SDTM Implementation Guide and define.xml metadata. Governs SAS dataset column type in regulatory submissions.
reference: CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide v3.4; CDISC Define-XML v2.1

description: Ordinal sequence number of this mapping rule within the parent SDTM dataset specification. Governs the order in which variables appear in the SDTM dataset and define.xml, and the execution order of transformation programs in SAS Drug Development.
reference: CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide; CDISC Define-XML v2.1

description: Name of the raw/staging dataset (SAS dataset or EDC extract table) that contains the source field prior to SDTM transformation (e.g., 'RAW_AE', 'RAW_VS'). Used in SAS Drug Development transformation programs to identify the input dataset for each mapping
reference: CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide; SAS Drug Development; FDA Study Data Technical Conformance Guide

description: Indicates whether this variable is mapped to a CDISC SDTM Supplemental Qualifier (SUPP--) dataset rather than the parent domain dataset (True). SUPPQUAL datasets hold non-standard variables that cannot be accommodated in the standard domain structure.
reference: CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide v3.4; CDISC Define-XML v2.1

description: Short variable name (QNAM) used in the SUPPQUAL dataset for this non-standard variable. Populated only when suppqual_flag is True. Must be uppercase, 1–8 characters, and unique within the SUPPQUAL dataset for the domain.
reference: CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide v3.4

description: Pinnacle 21 / CDISC conformance rule error or warning code associated with the most recent validation failure for this mapping (e.g., 'SD0083', 'SD0006'). Null when validation_status is 'passed' or 'not_validated'.
reference: CDISC Conformance Rules; Pinnacle 21; FDA Study Data Technical Conformance Guide

description: Current status of the CDISC Pinnacle 21 / OpenCDISC validation check result for this mapping rule. 'passed' indicates no conformance errors; 'failed' indicates outstanding validation errors requiring remediation before DBL; 'waived' indicates a documented
reference: CDISC Conformance Rules; FDA Study Data Technical Conformance Guide; Pinnacle 21

description: Unique surrogate identifier for the bioanalytical assay record in the lakehouse. Primary key. Entity role: MASTER_RESOURCE — represents a validated analytical method owned and managed by the bioanalytical laboratory.
reference: CDISC SDTM; FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance (2018)

description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.application. Business justification: A bioanalytical assay is developed and validated to measure a specific investigational compound or metabolite (pipeline asset).
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Foreign key linking to randomization.blinding_config. Business justification: GCP requires bioanalytical labs to operate under a defined blinding configuration — unblinded PK labs must be formally designated per blinding_config.
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Foreign key linking to document.document_sop. Business justification: GLP/GCP bioanalytical assays must reference their validated method SOP. Regulatory submissions (NDA/BLA bioanalytical section) and FDA/EMA inspections require direct traceability from
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Foreign key linking to supply.imp_master. Business justification: FDA/EMA bioanalytical method validation guidance requires each validated assay to be linked to the specific IMP it measures.
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Foreign key linking to study.investigational_product. Business justification: Bioanalytical assays are validated to measure specific investigational products.
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Foreign key linking to laboratory.lab_facility. Business justification: A bioanalytical assay is validated and performed at a specific laboratory facility.
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Foreign key linking to laboratory.lab_panel. Business justification: A bioanalytical assay (used for PK/PD/DMPK quantification) is associated with a specific lab panel definition — for example, a PK panel (is_pk_panel=true on lab_panel) maps to the
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Foreign key linking to study.protocol. Business justification: FDA bioanalytical method validation guidance requires protocol-specific assay validation documentation.
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Foreign key to the study this record belongs to, for study context and traceability.
Foreign key linking to study.study_protocol_amendment. Business justification: Protocol amendments frequently trigger new bioanalytical assay versions (new analyte, matrix change, updated LLOQ).
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.submission. Business justification: FDA and EMA require bioanalytical method validation reports in NDA/BLA submissions (FDA Guidance for Industry: Bioanalytical Method Validation).
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Foreign key linking to document.tmf_document. Business justification: Bioanalytical validation reports are TMF documents (DIA TMF Reference Model Zone 3, Section 3.2).
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Mean accuracy of the assay expressed as percent of nominal concentration (%Nominal) at QC levels during validation. Regulatory acceptance criterion is typically 85–115% (80–120% at LLOQ). Stored as the worst-case value across QC levels.
reference: FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance (2018); EMA Guideline on Bioanalytical Method Validation (2011); ICH M10

description: Broad classification of the analyte type measured by the assay. Distinguishes small molecule drugs (PK), large molecule biologics, biomarkers (PD), immunogenicity (anti-drug antibodies), metabolites, and endogenous compounds.
reference: FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance (2018); EMA Guideline on Bioanalytical Method Validation (2011); ICH M10

description: Name of the substance being measured by the assay (e.g., drug compound, metabolite, biomarker, anti-drug antibody). Directly links the assay to the pharmacokinetic (PK), pharmacodynamic (PD), or immunogenicity endpoint it supports.
reference: CDISC SDTM PC Domain; FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance (2018); ICH M10

description: Externally-known unique alphanumeric code assigned to the assay by the bioanalytical laboratory or sponsor (e.g., 'BA-LC-001', 'ELISA-TNF-003'). Used as the business identifier across CTMS, EDC, and regulatory submissions.
reference: FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance (2018); EMA Guideline on Bioanalytical Method Validation (2011)

description: Full descriptive name of the bioanalytical assay as used in study protocols, validation reports, and regulatory submissions (e.g., 'LC-MS/MS Assay for Compound XYZ in Human Plasma'). Satisfies MASTER_RESOURCE IDENTITY_LABEL category.
reference: FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance (2018); ICH M10 Bioanalytical Method Validation

description: Primary scientific purpose the assay serves within the clinical or nonclinical program. PK (Pharmacokinetics) assays measure drug concentration over time; PD (Pharmacodynamics) assays measure biological effect; Immunogenicity assays detect anti-drug
reference: CDISC SDTM PC/PP Domains; FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance (2018); ICH M10

description: Analytical technology platform used to perform the assay. Common types include LC-MS/MS (Liquid Chromatography-Tandem Mass Spectrometry), ELISA (Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay), ECL (Electrochemiluminescence), PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction), Flow
reference: FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance (2018); EMA Guideline on Bioanalytical Method Validation (2011); ICH M10

description: Mathematical regression model used to fit the calibration curve for back-calculation of analyte concentrations from instrument response. Common models include Linear (1/x or 1/x² weighting), Quadratic, 4-Parameter Logistic (4PL), and 5-Parameter Logistic
reference: FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance (2018); EMA Guideline on Bioanalytical Method Validation (2011); ICH M10

description: CDISC test code; implements SDTM PC.PCTESTCD
reference: CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide; CDISC Controlled Terminology; FDA SDTM Submission Requirements

description: Timestamp when the bioanalytical assay record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ (Attributable, Legible, Contemporaneous, Original, Accurate) data integrity principles.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+; ICH E6(R2) GCP; GDPR Article 5

description: Statistical method used to establish the screening and confirmatory cut points for immunogenicity (anti-drug antibody) assays (e.g., 'Parametric 5th percentile', 'Non-parametric 5th percentile').
reference: FDA Immunogenicity Testing Guidance (2019); EMA Guideline on Immunogenicity Assessment; ICH M10

description: Maximum validated dilution factor that can be applied to samples exceeding the ULOQ while maintaining assay accuracy and precision within acceptance criteria. Samples requiring dilution beyond this factor must be flagged.
reference: FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance (2018); ICH M10

description: Date after which the assay validation is no longer considered current and re-validation or re-qualification is required. Relevant for long-running studies where assay reagents, reference standards, or critical reagents may expire.
reference: FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance (2018); EMA Guideline on Bioanalytical Method Validation (2011); ICH M10

description: Indicates whether the assay is performed under Good Clinical Practice (GCP) standards as required for clinical trial sample analysis. True = GCP-compliant; False = non-GCP.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; EMA GCP Directive 2005/28/EC

description: Indicates whether the assay was validated and is performed under Good Laboratory Practice (GLP) regulations. GLP compliance is required for nonclinical safety studies submitted to regulatory agencies. True = GLP-compliant; False = non-GLP.
reference: GLP (21 CFR Part 58); OECD Principles of GLP; EMA GLP Directive 2004/10/EC

description: Between-run precision expressed as percent coefficient of variation (%CV) across multiple analytical runs during validation. Regulatory acceptance criterion is typically ≤15% (%CV). Stored as the worst-case value across QC levels.
reference: FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance (2018); EMA Guideline on Bioanalytical Method Validation (2011); ICH M10

description: Name or identifier of the internal standard (IS) used in the assay for quantification normalization (e.g., stable isotope-labeled analog, structural analog).
reference: FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance (2018); ICH M10

description: Within-run precision expressed as percent coefficient of variation (%CV) at the QC concentration levels, as determined during validation. Regulatory acceptance criterion is typically ≤15% (%CV), or ≤20% at LLOQ.
reference: FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance (2018); EMA Guideline on Bioanalytical Method Validation (2011); ICH M10

description: Lower Limit of Quantification — the lowest analyte concentration that can be reliably quantified with acceptable accuracy and precision per the validated method. Expressed in the unit defined by lloq_uloq_unit.
reference: FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance (2018); EMA Guideline on Bioanalytical Method Validation (2011); ICH M10; CDISC SDTM PC Domain

description: Unit of measurement for the LLOQ and ULOQ values (e.g., 'ng/mL', 'pg/mL', 'µg/mL', 'nM'). Must be consistent with the unit reported in PK/PD concentration data submitted to regulatory agencies.
reference: CDISC SDTM PC Domain; FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance (2018); ICH M10

description: Number of days for which analyte stability in the biological matrix at long-term storage conditions (typically -20°C or -70°C) has been validated. Samples stored beyond this period require re-validation of stability before results can be reported.
reference: FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance (2018); EMA Guideline on Bioanalytical Method Validation (2011); ICH M10

description: Indicates whether matrix effect (ion suppression/enhancement for LC-MS/MS; non-specific binding for LBA) was formally evaluated during validation. True = matrix effect experiments conducted; False = not assessed.
reference: FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance (2018); ICH M10

description: Specimen matrix type; implements SDTM PC.PCSPEC (CDISC CT SPECTYPE codelist)
reference: FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance (2018); EMA Guideline on Bioanalytical Method Validation (2011); ICH M10

description: Indicates whether parallelism (serial dilution of incurred samples producing results parallel to the calibration curve) was assessed. Relevant primarily for LBA and immunogenicity assays. True = parallelism assessed; False = not assessed.
reference: FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance (2018); EMA Guideline on Bioanalytical Method Validation (2011); ICH M10

description: Lot number of the certified reference standard used to prepare calibration standards and quality control (QC) samples. Traceability of the reference standard lot is required for regulatory submissions and audit purposes.
reference: FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance (2018); USP Reference Standards; ICH M10

description: Minimum volume of biological matrix (in microliters) required per sample aliquot for a single assay run. Used for specimen collection planning, biobank management, and feasibility assessment of retrospective analyses.
reference: FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance (2018); ICH M10; CDISC SDTM BS Domain

description: Indicates whether selectivity (absence of interference from endogenous matrix components) was formally assessed during validation. True = selectivity experiments conducted and documented; False = not assessed.
reference: FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance (2018); ICH M10

description: Biological species for which the assay has been validated. Assays validated in human matrices may differ from those validated in preclinical animal species used in DMPK studies. Drives applicability to clinical vs. nonclinical programs.
reference: FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance (2018); ICH M10; OECD GLP Principles

description: Sponsor-assigned identifier for the assay as referenced in the study protocol, the source system, or regulatory submission. May differ from the CRO's internal assay code. Required for cross-referencing sponsor documents with CRO laboratory records.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA IND (21 CFR Part 312); CDISC SDTM

description: Number of freeze-thaw cycles for which analyte stability in the biological matrix has been validated. Samples subjected to more freeze-thaw cycles than validated must be flagged or excluded from analysis.
reference: FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance (2018); EMA Guideline on Bioanalytical Method Validation (2011); ICH M10

description: Required storage temperature and conditions for samples analyzed by this assay (e.g., '-70°C ± 10°C', '-20°C', '2–8°C'). Defines the chain-of-custody storage requirement for clinical samples to maintain analyte integrity.
reference: FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance (2018); ICH M10; ICH Q1A Stability Testing

description: Assay code of the newer version that replaces this assay when it is retired or superseded. Supports version lineage tracking and ensures historical sample results can be linked to the correct assay version.
reference: FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance (2018); ICH M10; ALCOA+

description: Upper Limit of Quantification — the highest analyte concentration that can be reliably quantified within the validated dynamic range. Samples above ULOQ must be diluted and re-assayed. Expressed in the unit defined by lloq_uloq_unit.
reference: FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance (2018); EMA Guideline on Bioanalytical Method Validation (2011); ICH M10

description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to the bioanalytical assay record. Required for audit trail compliance under 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ data integrity principles. Tracks when assay parameters, validation status, or metadata were last changed.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+; ICH E6(R2) GCP; GDPR Article 5

description: Date on which the bioanalytical method validation was formally completed and the validation report was approved. Marks the point from which the assay is considered fit for regulated use in clinical sample analysis.
reference: FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance (2018); ICH M10; GLP (21 CFR Part 58)

description: Current regulatory validation tier of the assay. 'Validated' indicates full GLP/GCP-compliant validation per FDA/EMA/ICH M10 guidelines; 'Qualified' indicates fit-for-purpose qualification; 'Exploratory' indicates early-phase research use only; 'In
reference: FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance (2018); EMA Guideline on Bioanalytical Method Validation (2011); ICH M10; GLP (21 CFR Part 58)

description: Version identifier of the assay method (e.g., 'v1.0', 'v2.1'). Incremented when the assay undergoes method changes requiring partial or full re-validation. Enables traceability of which assay version was used for each study's sample analysis.
reference: FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance (2018); ICH M10; 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+

description: Statistical weighting factor applied to the calibration curve regression to minimize heteroscedasticity (e.g., '1/x', '1/x²', 'none'). Documented in the validation report and applied consistently during sample analysis.
reference: FDA Bioanalytical Method Validation Guidance (2018); ICH M10

description: Unique surrogate identifier for each bioanalytical or biomarker assay result record in the clinical trial laboratory data product. Serves as the primary key for the silver-layer lakehouse table.
reference: CDISC SDTM PC/PP Domain; 21 CFR Part 11

description: Foreign key linking to study.study_arm. Business justification: PK/PD exposure analysis by treatment arm is a core pharmacokinetic reporting requirement. Arm-level PK parameter comparisons (e.g., AUC, Cmax by dose group) are required for regulatory
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Foreign key linking to laboratory.bioanalytical_assay. Business justification: A bioanalytical result is produced by executing a specific validated bioanalytical assay.
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Foreign key linking to compliance.compliance_sop. Business justification: Bioanalytical result generation, review, and reporting must follow compliance SOPs (ICH M10 Section 7).
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Foreign key linking to consent.subject_consent. Business justification: Bioanalytical data sharing with third parties (CROs, partners, regulators) requires subject consent verification.
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Foreign key linking to biostatistics.database_lock_event. Business justification: Bioanalytical results are subject to database lock for PK analysis datasets.
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Foreign key linking to study.study_epoch. Business justification: PK/PD results must be epoch-stratified for NCA (single-dose vs steady-state epochs) and SDTM PC domain mapping.
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Foreign key linking to consent.consent_icf_version. Business justification: Bioanalytical results (drug concentration data) submitted in NDA/BLA packages must be traceable to the ICF version authorizing PK/PD sampling.
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Foreign key linking to laboratory.lab_facility. Business justification: A bioanalytical result is generated at a specific laboratory facility. The existing laboratory_code STRING column is a denormalized reference to lab_facility.
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Foreign key linking to supply.manufacture_batch. Business justification: FDA/EMA bioanalytical method validation guidance requires traceability from drug concentration results to the specific IMP manufacture batch.
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Reference to the biological specimen record from which this assay result was derived. Supports chain-of-custody traceability from collection through analysis.
reference: CDISC SDTM PC Domain PCREFID; 21 CFR Part 58 (GLP)

description: Foreign key linking to study.protocol. Business justification: Bioanalytical results require protocol-level traceability for NDA/BLA regulatory submissions (SDTM PC/PP domains). bioanalytical_result has study_id but not protocol_id.
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Foreign key linking to biostatistics.pk_analysis_spec. Business justification: Bioanalytical results are processed into PK parameters according to a specific PK analysis spec (LLOQ handling, NCA rules, exclusion criteria).
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Foreign key linking to laboratory.specimen_aliquot. Business justification: A bioanalytical result (PK/PD/DMPK) is produced from a specific specimen aliquot.
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Reference to the clinical study (protocol) under which this bioanalytical result was generated. Links the result to the governing protocol, sponsor, and regulatory context.
reference: CDISC SDTM IG v3.3; ICH E6(R2) GCP

description: Foreign key linking to study.study_protocol_amendment. Business justification: Bioanalytical results must reference the protocol amendment version active at analysis time for NDA/BLA submission traceability (SDTM PC domain).
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Foreign key linking to study.study_visit_schedule. Business justification: PK/PD bioanalytical results must be mapped to protocol-defined sampling visits for SDTM PC/PP domain generation and NCA analysis.
