description: Name and version of the software used to generate the randomization list (e.g., 'SAS 9.4', 'R 4.2.1', 'the source system 21.3'). Required for regulatory submission and reproducibility validation.
reference: ICH E9; 21 CFR Part 11; FDA Guidance on Computerized Systems

description: Comma-separated list of 3-letter ISO country codes where this randomization scheme is applicable (e.g., 'USA,GBR,DEU'). Relevant for multi-regional trials with country-specific regulatory requirements.
reference: ICH E9; EU CTR 536/2014; FDA IND; ISO 3166-1 alpha-3

description: Indicates whether a scheme amendment requires re-submission to the Institutional Review Board (IRB) or Independent Ethics Committee (IEC). Relevant when stratification factors or allocation ratios change.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 56; EU CTR 536/2014; OHRP

description: The scheme identifier or configuration reference as recorded in the IRT/RTSM system (e.g., the source system scheme ID or Medidata Rave RTSM list ID). Enables cross-system traceability.
reference: Oracle Clinical One; Medidata Rave RTSM; ICH E6(R2)

description: Name of the IRT/IVRS/RTSM system used to execute this randomization scheme (e.g., 'the source system 'Medidata Rave RTSM', 'Almac IXRS'). Identifies the operational system of record for subject allocation.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA Guidance on IRT/IVRS; Oracle Clinical One; Medidata Rave

description: Indicates whether randomization is performed centrally via IRT/IVRS/RTSM (True) or locally at the site (False). Centralized randomization is the standard for GCP-compliant multi-center trials.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA Guidance on IRT; Oracle Clinical One

description: Indicates whether randomization is stratified by investigative site. Site stratification is common in multi-center trials to ensure balance across sites.
reference: ICH E9 Section 2.3; FDA Guidance on Randomization

description: Indicates whether variable (random) block sizes are used rather than a fixed block size. Variable blocks reduce the ability to predict upcoming assignments and are preferred for double-blind studies.
reference: ICH E9; FDA Guidance on Randomization

description: Date on which the randomization list was generated using the specified software and seed. Required for audit trail and regulatory submission documentation.
reference: ICH E9; 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+

description: For minimization or covariate-adaptive algorithms, the mathematical objective function used to minimize imbalance across covariates (e.g., 'range', 'variance', 'weighted_range'). Null for non-minimization schemes.
reference: ICH E9; Pocock & Simon (1975); FDA Adaptive Design Guidance

description: For minimization algorithms, the probability (0.0–1.0) of assigning a subject to the arm that minimizes imbalance (e.g., 0.8000 = 80% biased coin). Null for non-minimization schemes.
reference: ICH E9; Pocock & Simon (1975); FDA Adaptive Design Guidance

description: Free-text field for additional operational notes, amendment rationale, or special instructions related to this randomization scheme. Not intended for structured data.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+

description: Numeric seed value used to initialize the pseudo-random number generator for reproducible list generation. Classified confidential to protect blinding integrity; disclosed only at database lock (DBL) or unblinding.
reference: ICH E9; 21 CFR Part 11; FDA Guidance on Randomization; EU CTR 536/2014

description: Indicates whether this randomization scheme version has been included in a regulatory submission (IND, NDA, BLA, MAA, or eCTD package). Triggers additional change-control requirements.
reference: FDA IND/NDA/BLA; EMA MAA; ICH CTD; eCTD

description: Date on which the randomization scheme was retired or superseded. Null if the scheme is still active. Used for version lifecycle management and TMF archival.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; TMF Reference Model; Veeva Vault eTMF

description: Version identifier of the Statistical Analysis Plan (the source system) that specifies this randomization scheme. Ensures traceability between the scheme implementation and the approved statistical methodology.
reference: ICH E9; CDISC ADaM; FDA SAP Guidance

description: Externally-known alphanumeric code uniquely identifying this randomization scheme within the RTSM/IRT system (e.g., the source system or Medidata Rave RTSM). Used as the business key for cross-system reference.
reference: Oracle Clinical One RTSM; Medidata Rave RTSM; ICH E9

description: Human-readable descriptive name of the randomization scheme (e.g., 'Phase III Stratified Block Randomization v2'). Used in reports, TMF documentation, and biostatistics deliverables.
reference: ICH E9; CDISC SDTM

description: Current lifecycle status of the randomization scheme. 'draft' = under development; 'approved' = biostatistics/QA sign-off obtained; 'active' = in use for subject allocation; 'suspended' = temporarily halted (e.g., DSMB hold); 'retired' = superseded or
reference: ICH E9; ICH E6(R2) GCP; Oracle Clinical One

description: Version identifier of the randomization scheme (e.g., '1.0', '2.1'). Incremented when the scheme is amended post-approval. Supports audit trail and regulatory submission traceability.
reference: ICH E9; 21 CFR Part 11; EU CTR 536/2014

description: Total number of distinct strata defined by the combination of stratification factors. Used to validate that the randomization list covers all strata and to monitor enrollment balance.
reference: ICH E9; SAP; Oracle Clinical One

description: Semicolon-separated list of stratification factors used to define strata for stratified randomization (e.g., 'site;gender;disease_severity'). Defined in the protocol and the source system. Null for non-stratified schemes.
reference: ICH E9 Section 2.3; CDISC SDTM; SAP

description: Total number of randomization positions (slots) generated in the scheme list. Represents the maximum number of subjects that can be randomized under this scheme version.
reference: ICH E9; Oracle Clinical One RTSM; Medidata Rave RTSM

description: Number of treatment arms (including placebo/control) defined in this randomization scheme. Must align with the protocol and allocation ratio.
reference: ICH E9; CDISC SDTM TA Domain; Protocol

description: Defines the authorized unblinding procedure for this scheme. 'emergency_only' = individual subject emergency unblinding; 'dsmb_only' = unblinding restricted to DSMB/DMC; 'dbk_full' = full unblinding at database lock; 'partial_sponsor' = sponsor
reference: ICH E9; ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA Guidance on Blinding; DSMB Charter

description: Timestamp of the most recent update to this randomization scheme record. Supports change tracking, audit trail, and version control in the silver layer.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+; ICH E6(R2) GCP

description: Unique surrogate identifier for the stratification factor record within the randomization scheme. Primary key for this entity.
reference: CDISC SDTM; ICH E9 Statistical Principles for Clinical Trials

description: Reference to the parent randomization scheme to which this stratification factor belongs. Each factor is owned by exactly one scheme.
reference: ICH E9; CDISC SDTM TA domain; Medidata Rave RTSM

description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.regulatory_protocol_amendment. Business justification: Stratification factors are frequently added, modified, or removed via protocol amendments.
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Reference to the clinical study for which this stratification factor is defined. Enables direct study-level filtering without joining through the scheme.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; CDISC SDTM; Oracle Clinical One

description: Target ADaM variable name for this stratification factor; implements ADaM variable reference (e.g., ADaM STRATxxx).
reference: CDISC ADaM Implementation Guide; FDA eCTD; SAS Drug Development

description: The date on which this stratification factor configuration was formally approved by the biostatistics or RTSM team. Required for regulatory audit trail and TMF documentation.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 11; Veeva Vault eTMF

description: Statistical method used to adjust for this stratification factor in the primary analysis: 'ancova' for Analysis of Covariance, 'cmh' for Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test, 'logistic_regression' for binary endpoints, 'none' if not used as a covariate in
reference: ICH E9; FDA Guidance on Covariate Adjustment (2023); CDISC ADaM; SAP

description: The date and time when this stratification factor record was first created in the data platform, in ISO 8601 format with timezone offset. Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ principles.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+; ICH E6(R2) GCP

description: Identifies the system or method from which the stratification factor value is captured at randomization: 'ecrf' from the EDC eCRF, 'ivrs' from Interactive Voice Response System, 'irt' from IRT/RTSM, 'central_lab' from laboratory results, 'manual_entry'
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; Medidata Rave EDC/RTSM; ALCOA+

business_glossary_term: Electronic Case Report Form (eCRF) Field Reference
description: The eCRF form and field identifier in the EDC system (e.g., Medidata Rave) from which the stratification factor value is sourced at the time of randomization (e.g., 'SCREENING.DISVSEV'). Enables traceability from randomization to source data.
reference: CDISC SDTM; 21 CFR Part 11; Medidata Rave EDC; ALCOA+

description: The date on which this stratification factor ceased to be effective for new randomizations, typically due to protocol amendment or study close-out. Null for currently active factors.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+

description: The date from which this stratification factor became effective for subject randomization, typically aligned with protocol approval or amendment effective date. Subjects randomized on or after this date are stratified using this factor.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+

description: Short, system-level alphanumeric code uniquely identifying the stratification factor within the scheme (e.g., REGION, DISEASE_STAGE, GENDER). Used as the programmatic key in RTSM/IRT configuration and SDTM mapping.
reference: CDISC SDTM; Medidata Rave RTSM; Oracle Clinical One

description: Detailed narrative description of the stratification factor, including its clinical rationale, how it is assessed, and its role in balancing treatment arms as documented in the Statistical Analysis Plan.
reference: ICH E9; FDA Guidance on Adaptive Designs; SAP

description: Human-readable name of the stratification factor as displayed in the RTSM/IRT interface and statistical analysis plan (e.g., 'Geographic Region', 'Baseline Disease Severity', 'Prior Treatment Status').
reference: ICH E9; CDISC SDTM; SAP (Statistical Analysis Plan)

description: Lifecycle status of the stratification factor within the scheme design workflow: 'draft' during initial configuration, 'approved' after biostatistics/RTSM sign-off, 'active' when live in the IRT system, 'suspended' during protocol amendment review
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; Medidata Rave RTSM; MasterControl; 21 CFR Part 11

description: Classification of the factor's measurement scale: 'categorical' for nominal groupings (e.g., region), 'continuous_binned' for numeric ranges converted to categories (e.g., age groups), 'ordinal' for ranked categories (e.g., disease severity), 'binary' for
reference: ICH E9; CDISC SDTM; FDA Guidance on Stratified Randomization

description: The exact parameter name as configured in the IRT/IVRS/RTSM system (e.g., Medidata Rave RTSM or the source system for this stratification factor. Used for system integration and UAT validation.
reference: Medidata Rave RTSM; Oracle Clinical One; ICH E6(R2) GCP

description: Indicates whether this stratification factor is currently active and in use for subject randomization (True) or has been deactivated via protocol amendment (False). Inactive factors are retained for historical traceability.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+

description: Indicates whether the stratification factor value is masked from unblinded personnel (True) or visible to all study team members (False). Relevant for double-blind studies where certain stratification criteria could reveal treatment assignment.
reference: ICH E9; ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA Guidance on Blinding

description: Indicates whether this factor is designated as a primary stratification factor (True) versus a secondary or exploratory factor (False) in the Statistical Analysis Plan. Primary factors are used in the primary efficacy analysis.
reference: ICH E9; SAP; FDA Guidance on Stratified Randomization

description: Indicates whether this stratification factor is included as a covariate in the primary statistical analysis model (True) or is used only for randomization balance without inclusion in the primary analysis (False).
reference: ICH E9; FDA Guidance on Covariate Adjustment; CDISC ADaM; SAP

description: Total number of enumerated levels (strata) defined for this stratification factor. Drives the dimensionality of the stratification matrix and the number of randomization lists required. For example, a 3-region factor has level_count = 3.
reference: ICH E9; CDISC SDTM; Medidata Rave RTSM

description: The maximum allowable imbalance (as a percentage or absolute count, per unit_of_imbalance) between treatment arms within any stratum defined by this factor before a balancing action is triggered in the minimization algorithm.
reference: ICH E9; FDA Guidance on Adaptive Designs; SAP

description: Specific variant of the minimization algorithm applied for this factor: 'pocock_simon' for the Pocock-Simon method, 'weighted_minimization' for factor-weighted minimization, 'biased_coin' for biased-coin minimization, 'deterministic' for deterministic
reference: ICH E9; Pocock-Simon (1975); FDA Guidance on Adaptive Designs

description: Numeric weight assigned to this stratification factor in a minimization or weighted minimization algorithm (e.g., Pocock-Simon). Values typically range from 0.0 to 1.0, with higher weights indicating greater influence on treatment allocation balance.
reference: ICH E9; Pocock-Simon Minimization Algorithm; FDA Guidance on Adaptive Designs

description: Defines the RTSM system behavior when the stratification factor value is missing or unknown at the time of randomization: 'block_randomization' to prevent randomization, 'assign_default_level' to use a pre-specified default level, 'flag_and_hold' to alert
reference: ICH E9; Medidata Rave RTSM; Oracle Clinical One; SAP

description: Free-text field for additional operational notes, biostatistician comments, or RTSM configuration remarks related to this stratification factor that do not fit into structured fields. Not used for regulatory submissions.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP

description: Reference to the specific section of the study protocol document that defines this stratification factor (e.g., 'Section 8.2.1 Stratification Factors'). Enables traceability from the data model to the governing protocol.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA IND Regulations 21 CFR 312; EU CTR 536/2014

description: The randomization algorithm applied in conjunction with this stratification factor: 'permuted_block' for block randomization within strata, 'minimization' for adaptive minimization, 'stratified_block' for stratified permuted block, 'dynamic_allocation'
reference: ICH E9; FDA Guidance on Adaptive Designs; CDISC SDTM

description: The native identifier assigned to this stratification factor within the source RTSM/IRT system (e.g., Medidata Rave RTSM internal factor ID or the source system factor GUID). Used for system integration, reconciliation, and audit trail linkage.
reference: Medidata Rave RTSM; Oracle Clinical One; 21 CFR Part 11

business_glossary_term: Randomization and Trial Supply Management (RTSM) System
description: Identifies the RTSM/IRT/IVRS system in which this stratification factor is configured and operationalized for subject randomization and kit assignment.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; Medidata Rave RTSM; Oracle Clinical One

description: Reference to the specific section of the Statistical Analysis Plan that describes the use of this stratification factor in primary and sensitivity analyses (e.g., 'the source system Stratification'). Supports regulatory audit traceability.
reference: ICH E9; FDA Guidance on SAP; CDISC ADaM

description: Target SDTM variable name for this stratification factor; implements SDTM variable reference.
reference: CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide; FDA eCTD Submission Standards; SAS Drug Development

description: Integer defining the display and processing sequence of this stratification factor within the randomization scheme. Lower values appear first in RTSM screens, the source system stratification matrix axes.
reference: Medidata Rave RTSM; Oracle Clinical One; CDISC SDTM

description: Specifies whether the max_imbalance_threshold is expressed as a 'percentage' of subjects within the stratum or as an absolute 'subject_count'. Determines how the RTSM system evaluates balance during randomization.
reference: ICH E9; Medidata Rave RTSM; SAP

description: The date and time when this stratification factor record was last modified in the data platform. Tracks configuration changes and supports change control audit trail under 21 CFR Part 11.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+; ICH E6(R2) GCP

description: Business rule or logical expression applied to validate the stratification factor value at the time of randomization (e.g., 'BMIBL >= 18 AND BMIBL < 30'). Prevents invalid factor assignments and ensures data integrity per ALCOA+ principles.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+; Medidata Rave RTSM; ICH E6(R2) GCP

description: Version identifier of this stratification factor definition, incremented with each protocol amendment or RTSM configuration change (e.g., '1.0', '2.0'). Supports change control and audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP; Medidata Rave RTSM; MasterControl

description: Primary key for kit_assignment

The unique transaction identifier generated by the IRT/IVRS/RTSM system (e.g., Medidata Rave RTSM) at the time of kit assignment. Serves as the business key for cross-system reconciliation and audit trail.
reference: Medidata Rave RTSM; Oracle Clinical One; ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 11

description: Foreign key linking to supply.kit_inventory. Business justification: kit_assignment (RTSM-driven) must reference the physical kit_inventory record to close the loop between RTSM assignment and physical IMP stock.
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Foreign key linking to randomization.rand_code. Business justification: A kit assignment corresponds to a specific randomization code slot. kit_assignment currently stores randomization_number (STRING) as a denormalized reference to the rand_code.
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Reference to the clinical study under which this kit assignment was made. Links the kit assignment to the parent study protocol.
reference: CDISC SDTM; ICH E6(R2) GCP

description: Reference to the investigational site where the kit was dispensed to the subject. Identifies the dispensing site for IMP accountability and supply chain tracking.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 312

description: Foreign key linking to study.study_visit_schedule. Business justification: Kit dispensing occurs at protocol-defined visits (is_dosing_visit flag in study_visit_schedule).
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Reference to the subject's randomization event that triggered this kit assignment. Establishes the link between the randomization domain and the supply/kit dispensing domain.
reference: CDISC SDTM; ICH E6(R2) GCP; RTSM system (Medidata Rave)

description: Foreign key linking to randomization.treatment_arm. Business justification: A kit assignment is made to a subject in a specific treatment arm. kit_assignment currently stores treatment_arm_code (STRING) and treatment_arm_description (STRING) as
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Reference to the enrolled study subject who received the IMP kit. Links the kit assignment to the subject randomization record for IMP accountability.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; CDISC SDTM DM domain

description: Reference to the scheduled or unscheduled study visit at which the IMP kit was dispensed to the subject.
reference: CDISC SDTM TV/SV domains; ICH E6(R2) GCP

description: Current lifecycle status of the kit assignment record, tracking the kit from initial assignment through dispensing, return, destruction, or loss. Essential for IMP accountability and regulatory compliance.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 5.13; 21 CFR Part 312.62; EU CTR 536/2014; CDISC SDTM EX domain

description: Categorizes the reason for the kit assignment: initial dispensing at randomization, resupply at a subsequent visit, replacement of a damaged/lost kit, dose titration, or rescue medication dispensing.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; Medidata Rave RTSM; Oracle Clinical One RTSM module

description: Indicates whether the kit assignment is blinded (treatment identity concealed), unblinded (treatment identity revealed, e.g., after emergency unblinding or study completion), or open-label.
reference: ICH E9 Statistical Principles; ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA Guidance on Blinding; CDISC SDTM

description: Free-text field for site staff or data management to record additional notes or observations related to the kit assignment event (e.g., reason for kit replacement, notes on subject compliance, dispensing anomalies).
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+ principles; 21 CFR Part 11

description: Indicates whether the subject demonstrated acceptable dosing compliance for this kit assignment based on the quantity dispensed versus quantity returned. True if compliance meets protocol-defined threshold; False if a compliance issue is identified.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; CDISC SDTM EX domain; FDA Guidance on Compliance; SAP (Statistical Analysis Plan)

description: The date and time when this kit assignment record was first created in the data system. Supports ALCOA+ audit trail requirements and data lineage tracking per 21 CFR Part 11 and ICH E6(R2) GCP.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+ principles; GDPR Article 5

description: Indicates whether the kit dispensing has been confirmed and acknowledged in the IRT/RTSM system by the site staff. True when confirmed; False when pending confirmation. Supports site monitoring and data quality checks.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 11; Medidata Rave RTSM; ALCOA+ principles

description: The calendar date on which the IMP kit was physically dispensed to the subject at the investigational site. Corresponds to the CDISC SDTM EXSTDTC (Exposure Start Date) and is critical for dosing compliance and PK/PD analysis.
reference: CDISC SDTM EX domain EXSTDTC; ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 312

description: The precise date and time at which the IMP kit dispensing transaction was recorded in the IRT/RTSM system. Supports ALCOA+ compliance (Attributable, Legible, Contemporaneous, Original, Accurate) for audit trail purposes.
reference: ALCOA+ principles; ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 11; Medidata Rave RTSM

description: Dose form; implements SDTM EC.ECDOSFRM/EX.EXDOSFRM; governed by CDISC CT dose form codelist.
reference: CDISC SDTM EX domain EXDOSFRM; ICH Q8 Pharmaceutical Development; FDA NDA/BLA requirements

description: The protocol-defined dose level associated with the kit (e.g., 'Low Dose', 'High Dose', '10mg', '50mg'). Supports dose-response analysis and PK/PD modeling. May differ from treatment arm in dose-escalation or titration studies.
reference: CDISC SDTM EX domain EXDOSE; ICH E9; FDA Guidance on Dose-Response Studies

description: Name of the IRT/IVRS/RTSM system that generated and recorded the kit assignment transaction. Important for multi-system studies and audit trail traceability.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 11; EU CTR 536/2014

description: The manufacturing batch or lot number of the IMP kit. Required for IMP accountability, pharmacovigilance investigations, and regulatory submissions. Enables traceability from subject exposure back to the manufacturing batch.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 5.13; 21 CFR Part 312.62; EU GMP Annex 13; CDISC SDTM EX domain

description: The expiration date of the IMP kit as labeled by the manufacturer or packaging facility. Ensures that expired kits are not dispensed to subjects and supports IMP accountability and supply chain management.
reference: ICH Q1A Stability Testing; 21 CFR Part 211.137; EU GMP Annex 13; ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 5.13

description: The unique alphanumeric identifier assigned to the investigational medicinal product (IMP) kit by the RTSM/IRT system or packaging facility. Used for IMP accountability and reconciliation across the supply chain.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 5.13; 21 CFR Part 312; EU CTR 536/2014; CDISC SDTM EX domain

description: Classification of the investigational medicinal product kit indicating whether it contains active IMP, placebo, comparator drug, rescue medication, or is open-label or blinded. Critical for treatment arm integrity and blinding management.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; CDISC SDTM EX domain; EU CTR 536/2014

description: Indicates whether a protocol deviation was associated with this kit assignment event (e.g., wrong kit dispensed, kit dispensed outside the protocol visit window, expired kit dispensed). True if a deviation is linked; False otherwise.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 4.5; FDA Guidance on Protocol Deviations; CDISC SDTM DV domain

description: The number of IMP units (e.g., tablets, vials, patches) dispensed to the subject as part of this kit assignment. Used for dosing compliance calculations and IMP accountability reconciliation.
reference: CDISC SDTM EX domain EXDOSE; ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 5.13; 21 CFR Part 312.62

description: The number of IMP units returned by the subject from this kit assignment. Used to calculate compliance (quantity dispensed minus quantity returned) and for IMP accountability at site level.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 5.13; 21 CFR Part 312.62; CDISC SDTM EX domain

description: The unique randomization number assigned to the subject by the IRT/IVRS/RTSM system at the time of randomization. Serves as the primary cross-reference between the randomization event and the kit dispensing record.
reference: CDISC SDTM RSUBJID; ICH E6(R2) GCP; Medidata Rave RTSM; Oracle Clinical One

description: The date on which the subject returned unused IMP units from this kit assignment to the investigational site. Null if no return has occurred or is not applicable.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 5.13; 21 CFR Part 312.62; EU CTR 536/2014

description: Indicates the current return status of the IMP kit: whether return is pending, the kit has been returned, the return requirement has been waived, or return is not applicable (e.g., fully consumed). Supports IMP accountability and site monitoring.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 5.13; 21 CFR Part 312.62; EU CTR 536/2014

description: Route of administration; implements SDTM EC.ECROUTE/EX.EXROUTE; governed by CDISC CT ROUTE codelist.
reference: CDISC SDTM EX domain EXROUTE; ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA NDA/BLA; WHO-DD

description: The value of the first stratification factor applied at randomization for this subject (e.g., 'Disease Severity: Mild', 'Region: North America'). Captured at the time of kit assignment to preserve the randomization context for statistical analysis.
reference: ICH E9 Statistical Principles; CDISC SDTM STRATCD; FDA Guidance on Adaptive Designs

description: The value of the second stratification factor applied at randomization for this subject (e.g., 'Prior Treatment: Yes/No', 'Age Group: <65/≥65'). Null if fewer than two stratification factors are defined in the protocol.
reference: ICH E9 Statistical Principles; CDISC SDTM STRATCD; FDA Guidance on Adaptive Designs

description: Subject identifier; implements SDTM DM.SUBJID; person-identifying (PII).
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; CDISC SDTM SUBJID; HIPAA; GDPR Article 4; 21 CFR Part 11

description: Indicates whether a temperature excursion was reported for this kit prior to or during dispensing. True if a temperature excursion was recorded; False otherwise. Relevant for temperature-sensitive IMPs and IMP accountability.
reference: ICH Q1A Stability Testing; EU GMP Annex 13; 21 CFR Part 211; ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 5.13

description: The date on which the kit assignment was unblinded, revealing the treatment arm identity. Populated only when blinding_status transitions to 'Unblinded'. Null for blinded or open-label assignments.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 4.7; FDA Guidance on Blinding; 21 CFR Part 312

description: The documented reason for emergency or planned unblinding of the kit assignment, if applicable (e.g., 'SAE requiring treatment knowledge', 'Study completion', 'DSMB review'). Null if the kit remains blinded.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 4.7; FDA Guidance on Blinding; CDISC SDTM

description: The date and time when this kit assignment record was last modified. Supports ALCOA+ audit trail requirements and change tracking per 21 CFR Part 11 electronic records regulations.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+ principles; GDPR Article 5

description: Unique surrogate primary key for each subject randomization or re-randomization event record in the Silver layer lakehouse.
reference: CDISC SDTM IG; 21 CFR Part 11

description: Foreign key linking to randomization.blinding_config. Business justification: A subject randomization event is governed by a specific blinding configuration that determines what information is masked.
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Foreign key linking to consent.subject_consent. Business justification: GCP requires randomization to occur only after documented informed consent. Linking subject_randomization to the specific subject_consent record that authorized randomization supports
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Reference to the version of the Informed Consent Form (ICF) that was in effect and signed by the subject prior to this randomization event. Ensures regulatory compliance that valid consent preceded randomization.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 4.8; FDA 21 CFR Part 50; EU CTR 536/2014; OHRP; GDPR Article 7

description: Foreign key linking to site.investigational_site. Business justification: GCP requires that the person performing randomization is formally assigned to the study with an authorized role.
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: The unique transaction reference number generated by the IRT/IVRS/RTSM system (Medidata Rave RTSM or the source system at the time of the randomization call. Used for audit trail reconciliation between the EDC and RTSM systems.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 5.5; ALCOA+ principles

description: For re-randomization events, the subject_randomization_id of the original randomization record that this event supersedes. Null for initial randomization events. Enables lineage tracing across re-randomization chains.
reference: ICH E9(R1) Addendum; CDISC SDTM DM domain; FDA Guidance on Adaptive Designs

description: Foreign key linking to study.protocol. Business justification: Each randomization event is performed under a specific protocol version; when a subject is randomized after a protocol amendment, the applicable version must be recorded for GCP compliance
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Foreign key linking to randomization.rand_code. Business justification: A subject randomization event consumes exactly one rand_code slot from the randomization list.
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Foreign key linking to randomization.rand_list. Business justification: A subject randomization event is performed against a specific randomization list version.
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

business_glossary_term: European Union Drug Regulating Authorities Clinical Trials (EudraCT) Number
description: EudraCT number assigned by the European Medicines Agency (EMA) for clinical trials conducted in EU/EEA member states. Required for EU CTR compliance and EudraCT/CTIS registration. Applicable only for EU countries.
reference: EU CTR 536/2014; EMA EudraCT; Directive 2001/20/EC

description: Date on which the country-level feasibility assessment was completed and the feasibility_score was assigned. Used to track the currency of feasibility data for enrollment planning.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; Oracle Siebel CTMS

description: Composite numeric score (typically 0–100) representing the overall feasibility assessment rating for conducting the study in this country, based on site availability, patient population, regulatory environment, and infrastructure.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; Oracle Siebel CTMS; Oracle Clinical One

description: Date on which the first investigative site in this country was activated and authorized to enroll subjects. Key milestone for country-level startup timeline KPI reporting in the source system
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; Oracle Siebel CTMS; CDISC SDTM

description: Date on which the first subject was enrolled (consented and randomized or screened) at any site within this country. Marks the start of active enrollment for country-level timeline tracking.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; CDISC SDTM DM domain; Oracle Siebel CTMS

description: Version identifier of the Informed Consent Form (ICF) approved by the national IRB/IEC and regulatory authority for use in this country. Ensures sites use the correct country-specific ICF version as tracked in Clinpal and Veeva Vault.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 4.8; FDA 21 CFR Part 50; EU CTR 536/2014; Clinpal

business_glossary_term: Institutional Review Board / Independent Ethics Committee (IRB/IEC) Approval Date
description: Date on which the national or central IRB/IEC granted ethical approval for the study to proceed in this country. Required before any subject enrollment can commence.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 3; FDA 21 CFR Part 56; OHRP; GDPR Article 9

business_glossary_term: Institutional Review Board / Independent Ethics Committee (IRB/IEC) Submission Date
description: Date on which the study protocol and informed consent materials were submitted to the national or central Institutional Review Board (IRB) or Independent Ethics Committee (IEC) for ethical review in this country.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 3; FDA 21 CFR Part 56; OHRP; EU CTR 536/2014

description: Date on which the last subject was enrolled in this country. Used to calculate country-level enrollment duration and to trigger enrollment completion milestones.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; CDISC SDTM; Oracle Siebel CTMS

description: Primary local language code for the country using IETF BCP 47 format (e.g., de-DE, ja-JP, fr-FR). Drives Informed Consent Form (ICF) translation requirements and eCRF localization in Clinpal and Medidata Rave.
reference: IETF BCP 47; ICH E6(R2) GCP; Clinpal; Medidata Rave

description: Country-specific regulatory reference or dossier number assigned by the national competent authority upon CTA/IND submission or approval (e.g., EudraCT number for EU, IND number for US, CTN for Australia). Stored in Veeva Vault.
reference: EU CTR 536/2014; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; TGA CTN; Health Canada; Veeva Vault

description: Country-specific clinical trial registry number assigned by the national registry (e.g., ISRCTN, UMIN for Japan, CTRI for India). Distinct from EudraCT and ClinicalTrials.gov identifiers. Required for WHO ICTRP compliance.

description: Target number of subjects planned to be enrolled in this country as defined in the study protocol and country feasibility assessment. Drives enrollment forecasting and country-level resource allocation.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; CDISC SDTM; Oracle Siebel CTMS; Oracle Clinical One

description: Planned number of subjects to be screened in this country, derived from the planned enrollment target and the assumed screen failure rate. Used for site capacity planning and patient recruitment forecasting.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; Oracle Siebel CTMS; Oracle Clinical One

description: Number of investigative sites planned to be activated in this country as defined in the study feasibility assessment and country-level enrollment plan. Used for resource planning and site activation tracking.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; Oracle Siebel CTMS; Oracle Clinical One

description: Indicates whether a regulatory hold (e.g., FDA Clinical Hold under 21 CFR 312.42, or equivalent national authority hold) is currently in effect for this country, preventing or suspending subject enrollment.
reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 312.42; EU CTR 536/2014 Article 35; ICH E6(R2)

description: Date on which the regulatory hold was lifted by the national authority, allowing enrollment to resume. Null if the hold is still in effect.
reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 312.42; EU CTR 536/2014; ICH E6(R2)

description: Narrative description of the reason for the regulatory hold in this country, as communicated by the national regulatory authority. Populated only when regulatory_hold_flag is True.
reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 312.42; EU CTR 536/2014; ICH E6(R2)

description: Date on which the regulatory hold was imposed by the national authority in this country. Used for regulatory timeline impact analysis and sponsor reporting.
reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 312.42; EU CTR 536/2014; ICH E6(R2)

description: Assumed proportion of screened subjects expected to fail screening criteria in this country, expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.3000 = 30%). Used in enrollment forecasting models to derive planned_screen_count from planned_enrollment_target.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; Oracle Siebel CTMS; SAS Drug Development

business_glossary_term: Subject Data Cross-Border Transfer Allowed Flag

reference: GDPR Chapter V; HIPAA; EU CTR 536/2014; ICH E6(R2)

description: Timestamp when this study-country record was most recently modified, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Supports ALCOA+ data integrity principles and change audit trail requirements per 21 CFR Part 11.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+; GDPR Article 5

description: Unique surrogate identifier for the dosing regimen record within the Clinical Trials data platform. Primary key for the dosing_regimen product in the study domain.

description: Reference to the study arm (treatment group) to which this dosing regimen applies. A study may have multiple arms each with distinct regimens (e.g., active drug arm vs. placebo arm).
reference: CDISC SDTM ARM; ICH E9 Statistical Principles

description: the pharmaceutical dose form from CDISC CT codelist FRM (C66726)
reference: CDISC SDTM EX.EXDOSFRM; CDISC Controlled Terminology; FDA NDA/BLA Labeling

reference: CDISC SDTM EX.EXTRT; ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 5.13; FDA 21 CFR Part 312

reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

business_glossary_term: CDISC ADaM Exposure (ADEX) Domain Mapping Notes
description: Notes describing how this dosing regimen maps to the CDISC ADaM ADEX (Analysis Dataset for Exposure) domain, including derivation rules for cumulative dose, dose intensity, and relative dose intensity calculations used in biostatistical analysis.
reference: CDISC ADaM ADEX Implementation Guide; CDISC Controlled Terminology; FDA Statistical Review Guidance; SAP

description: The allocation ratio of the dosing regimen.

Blinding level applied to this dosing regimen as defined in the study protocol (e.g., 'double-blind' where neither subject nor investigator knows the treatment assignment). Impacts RTSM/IRT dispensing logic and unblinding procedures.
reference: ICH E9 Statistical Principles; ICH E6(R2) GCP; CDISC SDTM TI Domain; FDA Guidance on Blinding

description: Indicates whether this regimen represents an active investigational product, placebo, vehicle control, sham procedure, or no-treatment arm. Critical for ITT and PP population definitions and regulatory benefit-risk assessment.
reference: ICH E9 Statistical Principles; ICH E10 Choice of Control Group; CDISC SDTM TA Domain; FDA Guidance on Placebo Controls

description: Timestamp when this dosing regimen record was first created in the data platform, conforming to ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ principles.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+ Principles; GDPR Article 5

description: Sequential step number within the dose escalation scheme (e.g., 1, 2, 3). Enables ordering of dose cohorts in escalation studies and supports dose-response curve construction in PK/PD modeling.
reference: CDISC SDTM EX Domain; FDA Guidance on Dose-Escalation Studies; ICH E9

description: Numeric dose amount to be administered per dosing event as specified in the protocol (e.g., 10.0, 50.5, 100.0). Represents the planned dose per administration. Used in PK/PD modeling and dose-response analysis.
reference: CDISC SDTM EX.EXDOSE; ICH E9 Statistical Principles; FDA Guidance on PK Studies

description: Narrative description of protocol-defined rules for dose modifications, reductions, interruptions, or discontinuations based on toxicity or adverse events (e.g., 'Reduce by 25% for Grade 2 AE; discontinue for Grade 3 SAE').
reference: CTCAE v5.0; ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.32; CDISC SDTM EX Domain

description: Number of permitted dose reduction levels defined in the protocol (e.g., 2 levels: Level -1 and Level -2). Used in oncology studies to manage toxicity while maintaining therapeutic benefit. Supports safety dose-response analysis.
reference: CTCAE v5.0; ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA Guidance on Oncology Drug Dosing

description: Frequency of dose administration using standard clinical abbreviations (e.g., 'QD' = once daily, 'BID' = twice daily, 'QW' = once weekly, 'Q2W' = every two weeks). Conforms to CDISC SDTM EX.EXDOSFRQ controlled terminology.
reference: CDISC SDTM EX.EXDOSFRQ; CDISC Controlled Terminology; ICH E9

description: Numeric interval between doses expressed in days (e.g., 1.0 for QD, 0.5 for BID, 7.0 for QW). Provides machine-readable precision for automated scheduling in RTSM/IRT systems and PK modeling when frequency alone is insufficient.
reference: CDISC SDTM EX Domain; Medidata Rave RTSM; ICH E9

description: Date on which this dosing regimen version ceased to be effective (e.g., superseded by an amendment). Null for currently active regimens. Supports temporal versioning and historical audit of regimen changes.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; EMA Clinical Trials Regulation EU CTR 536/2014

description: Date from which this dosing regimen version became effective in the study, typically aligned with protocol approval or amendment approval date. Supports temporal versioning of regimen changes across the study lifecycle.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; EMA Clinical Trials Regulation EU CTR 536/2014

description: Narrative description of the dose escalation scheme applied in this regimen (e.g., '3+3 design', 'Accelerated Titration', 'BOIN design', 'mTPI-2'). Populated only when is_dose_escalation = True. Supports Phase I safety and PK/PD analysis.
reference: FDA Guidance on Dose-Escalation Studies; ICH E9; CDISC SDTM EX Domain

description: Duration of intravenous or subcutaneous infusion in minutes, applicable when dosing_route is 'INTRAVENOUS' or similar. Null for non-infusion routes. Critical for PK modeling of IV drug exposure and site nursing procedure planning.
reference: CDISC SDTM EX.EXDUR; ICH E9; FDA Guidance on PK Studies

description: Indicates whether this regimen is part of a dose-escalation scheme (True) or a fixed-dose regimen (False). When True, the escalation_scheme_description and mtd_flag fields become operationally relevant. Common in Phase I oncology studies.
reference: ICH E9 Statistical Principles; FDA Guidance on Dose-Escalation Studies; CDISC SDTM EX Domain

description: Indicates whether this dose level has been designated as the Maximum Tolerated Dose (MTD) by the Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) or study team (True = MTD confirmed). Critical for Phase I dose-finding studies and regulatory submissions.
reference: FDA Guidance on MTD Determination; ICH E9; DSMB Charter; CDISC SDTM EX Domain

description: Number of days the loading dose is administered before transitioning to the maintenance dose. Null if no loading dose is defined. Supports PK/PD modeling of drug accumulation and steady-state calculations.
reference: CDISC SDTM EX Domain; ICH E9; FDA Guidance on PK Studies; DMPK principles

description: Initial higher dose administered to rapidly achieve therapeutic drug concentrations before transitioning to the maintenance dose level. Expressed in the same unit as dose_unit. Null if no loading dose is specified in the protocol.
reference: CDISC SDTM EX Domain; ICH E9; FDA Guidance on PK Studies; DMPK principles

description: Maximum allowable dose level for this regimen as defined in the protocol (e.g., dose cap for safety). Expressed in the same unit as dose_unit. Used in dose modification rules and safety monitoring.
reference: CDISC SDTM EX Domain; ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA Clinical Trials Regulation

description: Indicates whether pharmacodynamic (PD) biomarker assessments are required for subjects on this dosing regimen (True = PD assessments mandated per protocol). Supports PK/PD modeling and dose-response analysis.
reference: ICH E9; FDA Guidance on PD Studies; CDISC SDTM CE/FA Domains; SAS Drug Development

description: Indicates whether pharmacokinetic (PK) blood sampling is required for subjects on this dosing regimen (True = PK sampling mandated per protocol). Drives PK visit scheduling, sample collection logistics, and DMPK analysis planning.
reference: ICH E9; FDA Guidance on PK Studies; CDISC SDTM PC/PP Domains; SAS Drug Development

description: Total planned duration of the dosing regimen expressed in days as specified in the study protocol (e.g., 84 days for a 12-week treatment period). Used for treatment period planning, supply forecasting, and CDISC SDTM EX.EXENDY derivation.
reference: CDISC SDTM EX.EXENDY; ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312

description: Version of the study protocol under which this dosing regimen was defined or last amended (e.g., 'v1.0', 'v2.1'). Enables traceability of regimen changes across protocol amendments. Supports TMF/eTMF document management and regulatory audit trails.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 6; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; EMA Clinical Trials Regulation EU CTR 536/2014; Veeva Vault eTMF

description: Allocation ratio for randomization to this arm/regimen expressed as a colon-separated ratio (e.g., '1:1', '2:1', '1:1:1'). Used in RTSM/IRT configuration and statistical analysis plan (the source system) for sample size and power calculations.
reference: ICH E9 Statistical Principles; CDISC SDTM TA Domain; Medidata Rave RTSM; Oracle Clinical One

description: Externally-known alphanumeric code uniquely identifying this dosing regimen within the study protocol (e.g., 'REG-001', 'ARM-A-DOSE-1'). Used in protocol documents, eCRFs, and CDISC SDTM EX submissions.
reference: CDISC SDTM EX Domain; ICH E6(R2) GCP

description: Human-readable name of the dosing regimen as defined in the study protocol (e.g., 'Low Dose QD', 'High Dose BID', 'Placebo TIW'). Used in protocol documents, the source system, and CSR narratives.
reference: CDISC SDTM EX Domain; ICH E6(R2) GCP

description: Current lifecycle status of the dosing regimen within the study. 'draft' indicates protocol development; 'active' indicates currently administered; 'suspended' indicates temporarily halted (e.g., pending safety review); 'discontinued' indicates
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA Clinical Trials Regulation EU CTR 536/2014

business_glossary_term: CDISC SDTM Exposure (EX) Domain Mapping Notes
description: Notes describing how this dosing regimen maps to the CDISC SDTM EX (Exposure) domain variables, including any derivation logic, controlled terminology mappings, or special handling required for regulatory submission datasets.
reference: CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide EX Domain; CDISC Controlled Terminology; FDA eCTD Guidance; EMA eCTD Guidance

description: Initial dose amount at the start of the regimen, particularly relevant for titration or escalation regimens where the dose changes over time. Expressed in the same unit as dose_unit. Supports PK/PD baseline modeling.
reference: CDISC SDTM EX Domain; ICH E9; FDA Guidance on Dose-Escalation Studies

description: Label identifying the treatment period within the study to which this regimen applies (e.g., 'Period 1', 'Run-In', 'Maintenance', 'Extension'). Supports crossover and multi-period study designs. Maps to CDISC SDTM EX.EPOCH.
reference: CDISC SDTM EX.EPOCH; CDISC Study Design Model; ICH E9

description: Timestamp when this dosing regimen record was last modified in the data platform, conforming to ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Supports change tracking, audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11, and ALCOA+ data integrity principles.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+ Principles; GDPR Article 5

description: Duration of the washout period in days required between treatment periods in crossover studies, or between prior therapy and study treatment. Null for parallel-group designs. Supports PK carryover analysis and crossover study scheduling.
reference: ICH E9 Statistical Principles; CDISC SDTM EX Domain; FDA Guidance on Crossover Studies

description: Unique surrogate identifier for the investigational medicinal product (IMP) or investigational device record in the lakehouse silver layer. Primary key for this master resource entity.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; CDISC SDTM IG

description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.country_registration. Business justification: An investigational product may have existing country registrations (approved comparators, reference products).
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Foreign key linking to document.tmf_document. Business justification: The Investigational Medicinal Product Dossier (IMPD) / Investigator's Brochure is a DIA TMF Zone 4 essential document.
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.ind_application. Business justification: An investigational product is authorized for clinical use under a specific IND/IMPD.

description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.nda_bla_application. Business justification: For late-phase trials, the investigational product is the subject of an NDA/BLA.

description: Name of the active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) or active substance in the investigational product. May differ from the INN for novel compounds. Used in IMPD/IND CMC sections, pharmacovigilance, and SDTM datasets.

description: Chemical Abstracts Service (CAS) Registry Number uniquely identifying the active substance chemical structure. Used in regulatory submissions, safety data sheets, and cross-referencing with pharmacological databases.
reference: CAS Registry; FDA CMC Guidance; EMA IMPD Guideline

description: DEA controlled substance schedule classification for the investigational product (e.g., Schedule II, Schedule IV) or 'not_controlled' if not a controlled substance.
reference: DEA 21 CFR Part 1308; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; ICH E6(R2)

description: Timestamp when the investigational product master record was first created in the system, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11, ALCOA+ principles, and GCP compliance.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2); ALCOA+ Principles; GDPR Article 5

description: Current clinical development phase of the investigational product at the time of record creation or last update (e.g., Phase 1, Phase 2, Phase 3). Informs regulatory strategy, risk classification, and portfolio management.
reference: ICH E8; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; EMA Clinical Trials Regulation

description: Physical form of the investigational product as administered to subjects (e.g., tablet, capsule, solution for injection, lyophilized powder). Captured per CDISC SDTM EX domain and referenced in supply chain and pharmacy management.
reference: CDISC SDTM EX Domain; FDA Dosage Form Terminology; WHO Pharmaceutical Preparations

description: EMA-assigned product number for the investigational product as registered in the EU Clinical Trials Information System (CTIS) or EudraCT. Required for EU regulatory submissions and EU CTR 536/2014 compliance.
reference: EU CTR 536/2014; EMA CTIS; EudraCT

description: Date on which the investigational product was first administered to a human subject in any clinical study. Key milestone for regulatory timelines, development history, and portfolio analytics.
reference: ICH E6(R2); FDA IND Guidance; EMA IMPD Guideline

description: Qualitative description of the investigational product formulation including excipients, vehicle, and any special formulation characteristics (e.g., 'immediate-release tablet with microcrystalline cellulose', 'sterile aqueous solution pH 7.4').
reference: ICH Q8; FDA CMC Guidance; EMA IMPD Guideline

description: Sponsor-assigned internal drug or device code uniquely identifying the investigational product across all studies (e.g., ABC-1234). Serves as the externally-known business identifier referenced in protocols, supply chain, and regulatory submissions.

description: Version number of the current Investigational Medicinal Product Dossier (IMPD) or IND on file with the regulatory authority for this product. Tracked in Veeva Vault for regulatory submission management and amendment history.

description: Date on which the IND application (FDA) or equivalent regulatory authorization application was first submitted for this investigational product. Tracked in Veeva Vault for regulatory milestone reporting.

description: Free-text narrative description of the investigational product including its therapeutic purpose, background, and any additional context not captured in structured fields. Used in protocol background sections and regulatory submissions.

description: Current lifecycle status of the investigational product master record (e.g., active for ongoing studies, discontinued if development halted, superseded if replaced by a new formulation). Drives supply chain and regulatory workflow decisions.
reference: ICH E6(R2); Medidata Rave RTSM; Oracle Clinical One

description: Indicates whether the investigational product is used in a blinded (masked) study design (True) or open-label (False). Drives blinding and unblinding procedures in Medidata Rave RTSM and the source system randomization configuration.
reference: ICH E9; ICH E6(R2); FDA Guidance on Adaptive Designs

description: Indicates whether this product record represents a comparator (active control or placebo) rather than the primary investigational product (True = comparator). Enables differentiation of IMP vs. comparator in supply chain, SDTM, and safety reporting.
reference: ICH E6(R2); EU CTR 536/2014; CDISC SDTM EX Domain

description: Indicates whether this product record represents a placebo (True) rather than an active investigational product or comparator. Used in RTSM randomization configuration, supply chain, and SDTM EX domain coding.
reference: ICH E6(R2); CDISC SDTM EX Domain; Medidata Rave RTSM

description: Name of the pharmaceutical manufacturer or contract manufacturing organization (CMO) responsible for producing the investigational product. Referenced in the IMPD/IND CMC section and supply chain records in the source system
reference: ICH Q7 GMP; FDA 21 CFR Part 211; EMA GMP Guidelines; EU CTR 536/2014

description: Physical site or facility name and location where the investigational product is manufactured. Required for regulatory submissions (IND/IMPD) and GMP compliance tracking. Distinct from the manufacturer legal entity name.
reference: ICH Q7 GMP; FDA 21 CFR Part 211; EMA GMP Guidelines

description: Pharmacological mechanism by which the investigational product exerts its therapeutic effect (e.g., selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor, PD-1 checkpoint inhibitor). Captured in the IND/IMPD and referenced in the protocol background section.
reference: ICH E6(R2); FDA IND Guidance; EMA IMPD Guideline

description: FDA-assigned National Drug Code (NDC) number for the investigational product, if applicable. Used for US regulatory submissions, pharmacy dispensing records, and drug accountability tracking. May be absent for novel compounds not yet assigned an NDC.
reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 207; FDA NDC Directory

description: Free-text operational notes or comments regarding the investigational product record, such as special handling instructions, known stability issues, or interim regulatory communications. Captured by data management or regulatory affairs teams.
reference: ICH E6(R2); ALCOA+ Principles; 21 CFR Part 11

description: Description of the primary and secondary packaging configuration for the investigational product (e.g., 'blister pack of 10 tablets in a carton', 'single-use vial 10 mL in a kit'). Referenced in supply chain, pharmacy, and RTSM kit configuration.
reference: ICH Q8; FDA 21 CFR Part 211.94; EMA IMPD Guideline; Medidata Rave RTSM

description: Classification of the investigational product by modality type (e.g., small molecule, biologic, gene therapy, medical device). Drives regulatory pathway selection, storage requirements, and supply chain handling.
reference: FDA 21 CFR Parts 312/812; EMA Guideline on IMP; ICH Q6A/Q6B

description: Current regulatory approval status of the investigational product (e.g., approved for a different indication, purely investigational, withdrawn from market). Informs regulatory strategy, labeling requirements, and comparator sourcing decisions.
reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 312; EMA Regulation (EC) No 726/2004; ICH E6(R2)

description: Period in months after which the investigational product must be retested before continued use, applicable to active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) and certain formulations. Distinct from shelf life; used in supply chain and QC planning.

description: Approved shelf life of the investigational product in months from the date of manufacture, as established by stability studies and documented in the IMPD/IND. Drives expiry date calculation, supply planning, and resupply triggers in Medidata Rave RTSM.
reference: ICH Q1A Stability; FDA 21 CFR Part 211.137; EMA IMPD Guideline

description: Sponsor's internal product or compound code used in portfolio management systems, distinct from the IMP code used in clinical operations. Enables cross-referencing between clinical development and commercial product pipelines.
reference: ICH E6(R2); Sponsor SOPs; Oracle Siebel CTMS

description: Required storage conditions for the investigational product as specified in the IMPD/IND and product label (e.g., 'Store at 2–8°C, protected from light', 'Store below 25°C'). Critical for supply chain cold chain management and site pharmacy compliance.
reference: ICH Q1A Stability; FDA 21 CFR Part 211.142; EMA IMPD Guideline

description: Maximum acceptable storage temperature in degrees Celsius for the investigational product. Used by supply chain and site pharmacy to configure cold chain monitoring alerts and validate storage compliance.
reference: ICH Q1A Stability; FDA 21 CFR Part 211.142; WHO Technical Report Series

description: Minimum acceptable storage temperature in degrees Celsius for the investigational product. Used by supply chain and site pharmacy to configure cold chain monitoring alerts and validate storage compliance.
reference: ICH Q1A Stability; FDA 21 CFR Part 211.142; WHO Technical Report Series

description: Nominal strength or concentration of the active substance in the investigational product as labeled (e.g., '10 mg', '100 mg/mL', '5 mg/kg'). Captured in the IMPD/IND and referenced in supply chain, pharmacy, and SDTM EX domain.
reference: ICH Q6A; CDISC SDTM EX Domain (EXDOSE); FDA CMC Guidance

description: Unit of measure for the investigational product strength (e.g., mg, mg/mL, IU). Standardized per CDISC controlled terminology to enable cross-study comparisons and SDTM dataset generation.
reference: CDISC Controlled Terminology (UNIT); ICH Q6A; FDA CMC Guidance

description: Therapeutic or pharmacological class of the investigational product (e.g., oncology, cardiovascular, CNS, anti-infective). Used for portfolio analytics, regulatory strategy, and study feasibility assessments.
reference: WHO ATC; MedDRA SOC; FDA Pharmacologic Class

description: The unit in which the investigational product is dispensed to subjects at the investigational site (e.g., tablet, vial, kit, syringe). Used in RTSM dispensing records, drug accountability logs, and SDTM EX domain.
reference: CDISC SDTM EX Domain; Medidata Rave RTSM; ICH E6(R2)

description: Timestamp when the investigational product master record was last modified, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11, ALCOA+ principles, and change management tracking.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2); ALCOA+ Principles; GDPR Article 5

description: WHO Drug Dictionary (WHO-DD) drug code assigned to the investigational product for standardized drug coding in adverse event reporting, SDTM datasets, and regulatory submissions. Enables cross-study signal detection in the source system
