description: Indicates whether Source Data Verification was actually conducted for this subject visit during this monitoring visit. False indicates the subject visit was in scope but SDV was not completed (e.g., source documents unavailable).
reference: Internal - M:N Association Attribute

description: Status of Source Data Verification (SDV) for this visit, indicating whether the CRA has verified the eCRF data against source documents. Drives monitoring visit planning and risk-based monitoring decisions.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 5.18; FDA Guidance on Risk-Based Monitoring; Oracle Siebel CTMS

description: Unique surrogate identifier for each subject visit record in the Silver layer lakehouse. Primary key for the subject_visit data product.
reference: CDISC SDTM SV Domain; 21 CFR Part 11

description: Foreign key linking to consent.subject_consent. Business justification: GCP requires visit-level consent verification (subject_visit.informed_consent_verified already exists).
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

business_glossary_term: Electronic Case Report Form (eCRF) Form ID
description: Reference to the Electronic Case Report Form (eCRF) visit form in the EDC system (Medidata Rave) associated with this visit. Links visit scheduling metadata to the data collection form for completeness tracking.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; CDISC CDASH; Medidata Rave EDC

description: Foreign key linking to subject.enrollment. Business justification: A subject visit is performed within the context of a specific enrollment. One enrollment has many visits.
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Foreign key linking to study.study_epoch. Business justification: Each subject visit occurs within a study epoch. FK to study_epoch enables epoch-level visit compliance analysis, SDTM SV epoch derivation, and epoch-based data review in EDC.
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Reference to the trial participant (subject/patient) who performed or missed this visit. Core party reference for the transaction.
reference: CDISC SDTM SV Domain; ICH E6(R2) GCP; HIPAA; GDPR

description: Reference to the Principal Investigator (PI) or sub-investigator who conducted or supervised this visit at the investigational site. Required for regulatory accountability per GCP.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.53; EU CTR 536/2014

description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.regulatory_protocol_amendment. Business justification: ICH E6 GCP requires subject visits to be traceable to the protocol amendment version governing visit procedures and schedules at time of conduct.
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Foreign key to the study this record belongs to.
Reference to the investigational site where this visit was conducted or was scheduled to occur. Supports site-level visit compliance monitoring.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; Oracle Siebel CTMS

description: Foreign key linking to study.study_visit_schedule. Business justification: Each subject visit is an instance of a planned visit in study_visit_schedule. This FK enables visit window compliance reporting (planned vs actual day), protocol deviation
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.submission. Business justification: Billing milestones in study contracts are triggered by specific subject visit events (FPFV, LPLV, visit count targets). billing_milestone has visit_count_target confirming this.
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: The actual calendar date on which the subject attended the visit and assessments were performed. Maps to SVSTDTC in CDISC SDTM SV domain. Null if the visit was missed or not yet conducted. Principal real-world event date for this transaction.
reference: CDISC SDTM SV.SVSTDTC; ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 11

description: The actual calendar date on which the visit concluded, applicable for multi-day visits or inpatient stays. Maps to SVENDTC in CDISC SDTM SV domain. Null for single-day visits.
reference: CDISC SDTM SV.SVENDTC; ICH E6(R2) GCP

description: Timestamp when this subject visit record was first created in the source system or ingested into the Silver layer lakehouse. Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ principles.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+; ICH E6(R2) GCP

description: Status of eCRF data entry for this visit in the EDC system (Medidata Rave), indicating whether data collection has been initiated, is in progress, completed, locked, or frozen. Used for data management tracking and database lock readiness assessment.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; CDISC CDASH; Medidata Rave EDC; ALCOA+

description: Signed integer representing the deviation in days between the actual visit date and the planned visit date (actual minus planned). Negative values indicate early visits; positive values indicate late visits. Zero indicates on-schedule.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; CDISC SDTM SV Domain; FDA 21 CFR Part 312

description: Total duration of the visit in minutes from check-in to check-out as recorded in the CTMS or EDC. Used for site capacity planning, resource utilization analysis, and subject burden assessment.
reference: Oracle Siebel CTMS; ICH E6(R2) GCP

description: Reason for early termination of the visit or the subject's participation, applicable when visit_type is 'early_termination'. Captures clinical, safety, or administrative reasons per protocol requirements.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; CDISC SDTM DS Domain

description: Indicates whether a valid, signed Informed Consent Form (ICF) was confirmed on file prior to this visit (True) or not (False). Critical GCP compliance requirement; absence may constitute a major protocol deviation.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 4.8; FDA 21 CFR Part 50; EU CTR 536/2014; OHRP

description: Indicates whether this visit was a protocol-scheduled visit (True) or an unscheduled/ad-hoc visit not defined in the protocol schedule of assessments (False). Unscheduled visits may indicate safety events or protocol deviations.
reference: CDISC SDTM SV Domain; ICH E6(R2) GCP

description: Indicates whether the treatment assignment was unblinded at or prior to this visit (True) or the subject remained blinded (False). Relevant for double-blind studies and impacts data integrity assessments.
reference: ICH E9(R1) Statistical Principles; ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312

description: Free-text or coded reason explaining why a scheduled visit was missed by the subject (e.g., subject unavailable, adverse event, travel, withdrew consent, site closure). Populated only when visit_status is 'missed'.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; CDISC SDTM SV Domain

description: Standardized coded value for the reason a scheduled visit was missed, aligned with sponsor or protocol-defined coding scheme. Complements missed_reason free text for structured analytics and regulatory submissions.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; CDISC SDTM SV Domain; MedDRA

description: Free-text clinical or operational notes recorded by the site staff or CRA regarding this visit, including observations about subject condition, procedural issues, or site-specific circumstances. Sourced from the source system or Medidata Rave.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; Oracle Siebel CTMS; Medidata Rave EDC

description: The target date on which the visit was scheduled to occur per the protocol-defined visit schedule, calculated from the subject's reference date (e.g., randomization date or first dose date). Used to compute visit window compliance.
reference: CDISC SDTM SV.SVSTDTC; ICH E6(R2) GCP

description: Indicates whether this visit resulted in a protocol deviation (True), such as a visit outside the allowed window, missed required assessments, or procedural non-compliance. Triggers downstream protocol deviation record creation in the compliance domain.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; EU CTR 536/2014

description: Number of open data discrepancy queries (DCFs) associated with this visit's eCRF data in the EDC system. Used for data quality monitoring and site performance tracking. Non-zero values may block database lock.
reference: ALCOA+; ICH E6(R2) GCP; Medidata Rave EDC; CDISC CDASH

description: The native primary key or unique identifier for this visit record in the originating source system (e.g., Medidata Rave visit OID, Siebel CTMS visit row ID).
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+; CDISC SDTM SV Domain

description: The relative study day on which the visit occurred, calculated from the subject's reference start date per CDISC convention (Day 1 = reference date; Day -1 = day before; no Day 0). Maps to SVSTDY in CDISC SDTM SV domain.
reference: CDISC SDTM SV.SVSTDY; CDISC SDTM Implementation Guide

description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to this subject visit record in the source system or Silver layer. Required for change tracking, audit trail compliance, and incremental data pipeline processing.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+; ICH E6(R2) GCP

description: Protocol-defined alphanumeric code uniquely identifying the visit within the study schedule (e.g., SCR, BL, V01, V02, ET, EOS). Maps to VISITNUM/VISIT in CDISC SDTM SV domain. Used as the externally-known business identifier for the visit.
reference: CDISC SDTM SV.VISIT; Medidata Rave EDC

description: Sequential numeric identifier for the visit as defined in the study protocol schedule of assessments. Maps directly to VISITNUM in CDISC SDTM SV domain. Used for ordering visits chronologically within a subject's participation.
reference: CDISC SDTM SV.VISITNUM; ICH E6(R2)

description: Current completion status of the visit indicating whether the subject attended and completed all required assessments, missed the visit entirely, partially completed assessments, had the visit rescheduled, or the visit was cancelled.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; Oracle Siebel CTMS; Medidata Rave EDC

description: Classification of the visit by its role in the study protocol lifecycle. Drives SDTM SV domain population and visit compliance analytics. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: screening|baseline|treatment|follow_up|unscheduled|early_termination|end_of_study — promote to
reference: CDISC SDTM SV Domain; ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312

description: The nominal study week associated with this visit as defined in the protocol schedule of assessments (e.g., Week 1, Week 4, Week 12). Used for time-point labeling in biostatistical analyses and ADaM dataset derivations.
reference: CDISC ADaM; CDISC SDTM SV Domain; ICH E9

description: The latest acceptable date for the visit to occur per the protocol-defined visit window (planned date plus the allowed late deviation in days). Used to determine visit window compliance status.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; CDISC SDTM SV Domain; FDA 21 CFR Part 312

description: Indicates whether the actual visit date fell within the protocol-defined visit window, occurred early (before window open), occurred late (after window close), was missed entirely, or is not applicable (e.g., unscheduled visits).
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; CDISC SDTM SV Domain

description: The earliest acceptable date for the visit to occur per the protocol-defined visit window (planned date minus the allowed early deviation in days). Used to determine visit window compliance status.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; CDISC SDTM SV Domain; FDA 21 CFR Part 312

description: Unique system-generated identifier for the clinical supply depot. Primary key for the depot master record.
reference: ICH Q10 Pharmaceutical Quality System; 21 CFR Part 211

description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.clinical_trial_authorization. Business justification: Depots holding IMP in a given country must operate under a valid CTA for that jurisdiction.
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Foreign key linking to document.document_sop. Business justification: Depot qualification, storage, and handling operations are governed by GMP/GCP SOPs. Linking depot to document_sop enables audit trail verification that the correct SOP version governed
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Foreign key linking to laboratory.lab_facility. Business justification: Depot 3PL providers are engaged via subcontracts that govern service obligations, GMP requirements, and liability.
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Foreign key linking to document.regulatory_binder. Business justification: Depot import licenses, wholesale distribution licenses, and GMP certificates are filed in regulatory binders.
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Foreign key to the study this record belongs to.

Foreign key linking to document.tmf_document. Business justification: Depot qualification reports and GMP certificates are ICH GCP essential TMF documents (Zone 5). Each depot must link to its qualification/GMP certificate document in the eTMF.
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Primary street address of the depot facility. Used for logistics routing, regulatory filings, and cold-chain shipment documentation.
reference: GDPR Article 4; ICH Q10; EU GMP Annex 13

description: Secondary address detail (suite, building, floor) for the depot facility.
reference: GDPR Article 4; ICH Q10

description: Total ambient temperature storage capacity of the depot measured in cubic metres. Ambient storage is typically 15–25°C. Used for supply planning and capacity allocation across studies.
reference: ICH Q1A Stability Guidelines; EU GMP Annex 13; USP <1079>

description: City in which the depot facility is located. Used for geographic distribution planning and regulatory jurisdiction determination.
reference: ICH Q10; EU GMP Annex 13

description: Indicates whether the depot has been formally qualified for cold-chain IMP handling, including validated temperature monitoring, qualified packaging, and trained personnel per WHO and GDP guidelines.
reference: WHO TRS 961 Annex 9; EU GDP Guidelines 2013/C 343/01; ICH Q1A

description: Indicates whether the depot is licensed to store and handle controlled substances (narcotics, psychotropics) as defined by DEA Schedule (US), Home Office (UK), or equivalent national authority.
reference: DEA 21 CFR Part 1301; UK Misuse of Drugs Regulations 2001; UN Convention on Psychotropic Substances

description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 three-letter country code for the country in which the depot is located. Drives regulatory jurisdiction, import/export rules, and cold-chain routing logic.
reference: ISO 3166-1; ICH Q10; EU GMP Annex 13; FDA 21 CFR Part 211

description: Timestamp when the depot master record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ data integrity principles.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+; GDPR Article 5

business_glossary_term: Clinical Trial Management System (CTMS) Depot ID
description: Depot identifier as recorded in the source system Enables cross-system reconciliation between the supply chain data product and clinical trial management records.
reference: Oracle Siebel CTMS; ICH E6(R2) GCP

description: Date on which the depot was or is scheduled to be decommissioned and removed from the active clinical supply network. Null for currently active depots.
reference: ICH Q10; EU GMP Annex 13

description: Externally-known alphanumeric code uniquely identifying the depot within the clinical supply network. Used in RTSM (Randomization and Trial Supply Management) and CTMS for depot referencing across studies.
reference: CDISC CDASH; ICH Q10

description: Full legal or operational name of the clinical supply depot as registered with regulatory authorities and used in the Trial Master File (TMF).
reference: ICH Q10; EU GMP Annex 13; 21 CFR Part 211

description: Current operational lifecycle status of the depot. Active depots are approved for IMP storage and distribution. Suspended depots are temporarily halted pending investigation or re-qualification. Decommissioned depots are permanently closed.
reference: ICH Q10; EU GMP Annex 13; 21 CFR Part 211.68

description: Classification of the depot within the clinical supply logistics network. Central depots serve as primary distribution hubs; regional depots serve geographic clusters; local depots are near investigational sites; satellite depots are temporary; returns
reference: ICH Q10; EU GMP Annex 13

description: Indicates whether the depot is authorized to perform on-site destruction of expired, returned, or unusable IMPs in compliance with GMP and environmental regulations.
reference: EU GMP Annex 13; ICH Q10; 21 CFR Part 312.62; EPA Hazardous Waste Regulations

description: Vendor or supplier identifier for the depot as registered in the source system for purchase order processing, invoice matching, and financial reconciliation of depot service fees.
reference: SAP S/4HANA; SOX Section 404; ICH Q10

description: Total frozen storage capacity (typically -20°C or -80°C) of the depot in cubic metres. Required for biologics, gene therapies, and other temperature-sensitive IMPs.
reference: ICH Q1A; EU GMP Annex 13; USP <1079>; WHO TRS 961 Annex 9

business_glossary_term: Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) Certificate Expiry Date
description: Date on which the depot's GMP certificate expires. Triggers re-qualification workflows and may suspend depot operations if not renewed prior to expiry.
reference: ICH Q10; EU GMP Annex 13; 21 CFR Part 211; EMA

description: Official certificate number issued by the regulatory authority confirming GMP compliance for the depot. Referenced in regulatory submissions and audit documentation.
reference: ICH Q10; EU GMP Annex 13; EMA; MHRA; TGA

description: Indicates whether the depot holds a current Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) certification as required for IMP storage and handling under ICH Q7/Q10 and applicable regional regulations.
reference: ICH Q7; ICH Q10; EU GMP Annex 13; 21 CFR Part 211; EMA GMP Guidelines

description: Expiry date of the depot's import license for IMP receipt. Expired licenses block inbound international shipments.
reference: ICH Q10; EU GMP Annex 13; FDA; PMDA

description: Date of the most recent GMP/GDP audit conducted at the depot by the sponsor, CRO, or regulatory authority. Audit outcomes are tracked in the quality management system (MasterControl).
reference: ICH Q10; EU GMP Annex 13; 21 CFR Part 211; ISO 9001

description: Date on which the depot last completed a formal qualification or re-qualification exercise (IQ/OQ/PQ). Qualification records are maintained in the eTMF and are subject to regulatory inspection.
reference: ICH Q10; EU GMP Annex 15; 21 CFR Part 211.68; ISPE GAMP 5

description: Scheduled date for the next GMP/GDP audit at the depot. Used for audit planning and compliance calendar management.
reference: ICH Q10; EU GMP Annex 13; 21 CFR Part 211

description: Scheduled date for the next depot qualification or re-qualification. Drives preventive maintenance and compliance calendar in the CTMS and quality management system.
reference: ICH Q10; EU GMP Annex 15; 21 CFR Part 211.68

description: Free-text field for operational notes, special handling instructions, or depot-specific constraints relevant to clinical supply operations. Not intended for regulatory documentation.
reference: ICH Q10

description: Date on which the depot became operationally active for clinical supply activities. Used for lifecycle tracking and regulatory documentation.
reference: ICH Q10; EU GMP Annex 13

description: Postal or ZIP code of the depot facility. Used for logistics routing and regulatory jurisdiction mapping.
reference: ICH Q10

description: Email address of the primary operational contact at the depot. Used for shipment alerts, RTSM notifications, and supply chain communications.
reference: GDPR Article 4; ICH Q10

description: Full name of the primary operational contact person at the depot. Used for logistics coordination, shipment notifications, and regulatory correspondence.
reference: ICH Q10; EU GMP Annex 13

description: Primary telephone number for the depot operational contact. Used for urgent logistics coordination and cold-chain incident escalation.
reference: GDPR Article 4; ICH Q10

description: Total refrigerated storage capacity (typically 2–8°C) of the depot in cubic metres. Critical for IMPs requiring cold-chain management.
reference: ICH Q1A; EU GMP Annex 13; USP <1079>; WHO TRS 961 Annex 9

description: Indicates whether the depot is authorized to receive returned Investigational Medicinal Products (IMPs) from investigational sites. Required for accountability reconciliation and destruction workflows.
reference: EU GMP Annex 13; ICH Q10; 21 CFR Part 312.62

business_glossary_term: Randomization and Trial Supply Management (RTSM) Depot Code
description: Depot identifier as configured in the RTSM system (Medidata Rave RTSM). Used to link depot master records to RTSM dispensing, randomization kit assignment, and resupply trigger logic.
reference: Medidata Rave RTSM; CDISC CDASH; ICH E6(R2) GCP

description: State, province, or administrative region where the depot is located. Relevant for import/export licensing and regional regulatory compliance.
reference: ICH Q10; 21 CFR Part 211

description: Name or model of the continuous temperature monitoring system installed at the depot (e.g., Sensitech TempTale, Berlinger ELPRO). Ensures 21 CFR Part 11 compliant electronic records of storage conditions.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; EU GDP Guidelines; WHO TRS 961 Annex 9; ICH Q1A

description: IANA time zone identifier for the depot location (e.g., America/New_York, Europe/London). Used for scheduling shipment windows, expiry checks, and operational hours alignment.
reference: IANA Time Zone Database; ICH Q10

description: Timestamp of the most recent update to the depot master record. Supports change tracking and audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ principles.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+; GDPR Article 5

description: Expiry date of the wholesale distribution license. Depot cannot legally distribute IMPs after this date without renewal.
reference: EU GDP Guidelines 2013/C 343/01; MHRA; 21 CFR Part 205

description: Unique surrogate identifier for each kit inventory record in the Databricks Silver Layer. Primary key for this data product.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP

description: Foreign key linking to study.study_arm. Business justification: Kit inventory is allocated by treatment arm for blinded and open-label studies. Linking kit_inventory to study.study_arm enables arm-level inventory accountability reporting, supports
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.clinical_trial_authorization. Business justification: Individual kit inventory items must be traceable to the CTA authorizing their dispensing at a given site/country.
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Reference to the supply depot or central warehouse currently holding this kit. Null when the kit has been shipped to a site.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; EU GMP Annex 13

description: Foreign key linking to document.document_sop. Business justification: Kit inventory management, storage, and handling procedures are governed by GCP SOPs. Linking kit_inventory to document_sop enables GCP compliance audits and inspection readiness
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Foreign key linking to study.dosing_regimen. Business justification: Kit inventory allocation is driven by the dosing regimen — the number of kits needed per subject per visit depends on dose frequency and duration.
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Foreign key linking to subject.enrollment. Business justification: Kit allocation to a subject must be traceable to the specific enrollment episode for IMP accountability.
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Foreign key linking to supply.kit_definition. Business justification: Each physical kit instance (kit_inventory) is manufactured according to a specific kit definition (kit_definition).
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Foreign key linking to supply.manufacture_batch. Business justification: Each physical kit instance belongs to a specific manufacturing batch (kit_inventory.batch_number is denormalized).
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Foreign key linking to randomization.rand_code. Business justification: rand_code is the authoritative RTSM record linking kit_code to treatment_arm and randomization slot.
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Reference to the inbound or outbound shipment record associated with the most recent logistics movement of this kit.
reference: EU GMP Annex 13; ICH Q10

description: Foreign key to the study this record belongs to.
Reference to the investigational site currently holding or assigned to receive this kit. Used for site-level inventory tracking and accountability.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312

description: Foreign key linking to randomization.subject_randomization. Business justification: IMP accountability regulations (ICH E6 GCP) require tracing each physical kit to the randomization event that triggered its dispensing.
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Reference to the enrolled subject to whom this kit has been dispensed. Null when the kit has not yet been assigned or dispensed to a subject.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; CDISC SDTM DM domain

description: Indicates whether this kit has been fully reconciled in the drug accountability log, confirming that dispensed, returned, and destroyed quantities are accounted for. Required for study close-out and regulatory inspection readiness.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; EU GMP Annex 13; ALCOA+

description: The manufacturing batch or lot number of the IMP contained in this kit. Essential for batch recall management, drug accountability, and regulatory submissions. Sourced from the Certificate of Analysis (CoA).
reference: EU GMP Annex 13; FDA 21 CFR Part 211.68; ICH Q7; 21 CFR Part 312

description: Indicates whether the kit identity (treatment assignment) is blinded, unblinded, or open-label for this record. Critical for maintaining study integrity and controlling access to treatment assignment information.
reference: ICH E9; ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312

description: Indicates whether the kit has maintained cold-chain compliance throughout its custody chain based on temperature monitoring data. A value of False triggers a quality investigation before dispensing.
reference: EU GMP Annex 13; WHO TRS 961; FDA Guidance on Temperature-Sensitive Drug Products; ICH E6(R2) GCP

description: Indicates whether this kit requires cold-chain storage and transportation (e.g., 2–8°C refrigeration or frozen conditions). Drives logistics planning, temperature monitoring requirements, and qualified packaging selection.
reference: EU GMP Annex 13; WHO Technical Report Series 961 (Cold Chain); FDA Guidance on Temperature-Sensitive Drug Products; ICH Q1A

description: Free-text field for site staff or supply chain personnel to record notes about this kit, such as reasons for quarantine, partial dispensing explanations, or deviation observations. Supports ALCOA+ documentation requirements.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+; 21 CFR Part 11

description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code of the country where this kit is currently located or was last recorded. Used for import/export compliance, country-specific labeling requirements, and regional supply planning.
reference: ISO 3166-1; EU CTR 536/2014; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; ICH E6(R2) GCP

description: The date and time at which this kit inventory record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ principles.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+; GDPR Article 5

description: Categorical indicator of where the kit physically resides in the supply chain at the current point in time. Used in conjunction with depot_id or site_id to determine precise location.
reference: EU GMP Annex 13; ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312

description: The date and time at which the kit was received at the supply depot from the manufacturer or another depot. Initiates the depot inventory record and chain-of-custody tracking.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+; EU GMP Annex 13; 21 CFR Part 11

description: The date and time at which the kit was confirmed destroyed per the destruction certificate. Required for drug accountability reconciliation and regulatory close-out documentation.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; EU GMP Annex 13; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; ALCOA+

description: The reference number of the official destruction certificate issued upon confirmed destruction of the kit. Required for drug accountability close-out and regulatory submission documentation.
reference: EU GMP Annex 13; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; ICH E6(R2) GCP

description: The actual number of dosage units dispensed to the subject from this kit. Used for drug accountability reconciliation and compliance with protocol-specified dosing.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; EU GMP Annex 13

description: The date and time at which this kit was physically dispensed to the subject by site staff. Captured in RTSM (Medidata Rave) as part of the chain-of-custody audit trail. Conforms to ALCOA+ contemporaneous documentation requirements.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+; 21 CFR Part 11; CDISC SDTM EX domain

description: The protocol-defined visit name or number at which this kit was dispensed to the subject (e.g., 'Visit 2 - Week 4'). Used for protocol compliance verification and eCRF reconciliation.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; CDISC SDTM EX domain; CDISC CDASH

description: The expiration date of the investigational medicinal product within this kit as printed on the label. Kits must not be dispensed after this date. Used for expiry management, re-supply planning, and regulatory accountability.
reference: EU GMP Annex 13; FDA 21 CFR Part 211.137; ICH Q1A Stability; ICH E6(R2) GCP

description: Externally-known unique alphanumeric identifier assigned to the physical randomization kit by the RTSM (Medidata Rave). This is the primary business identifier used in drug accountability logs, dispensing records, and regulatory submissions.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; CDISC CDASH; EU GMP Annex 13; FDA 21 CFR Part 312

description: Current lifecycle status of the kit within the supply chain. 'available' = at depot or site, ready for assignment; 'assigned' = allocated to a subject via RTSM but not yet dispensed; 'dispensed' = physically given to subject; 'expired' = past expiry date
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; EU GMP Annex 13; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; ALCOA+

description: The version identifier of the IMP label applied to this kit. Used to verify that the correct, IRB/IEC-approved label version was used at the time of dispensing and for regulatory label reconciliation.
reference: EU GMP Annex 13; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.6; ICH E6(R2) GCP; EU CTR 536/2014

description: Date on which the investigational medicinal product in this kit was manufactured. Used for shelf-life calculation, batch traceability, and regulatory accountability.
reference: EU GMP Annex 13; FDA 21 CFR Part 211; ICH Q7

description: The version of the study protocol under which this kit was dispensed or assigned. Ensures that kit dispensing is traceable to the correct protocol amendment for regulatory compliance.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; EU CTR 536/2014; CDISC SDTM

description: The unique randomization number assigned to the subject-kit pairing by the RTSM (IRT/IVRS) at the point of subject randomization. Links the kit to the randomization schedule for unblinding and accountability.
reference: ICH E9; ICH E6(R2) GCP; CDISC SDTM RANDO; FDA 21 CFR Part 312

description: Date by which the kit must be retested or re-evaluated for continued use, particularly for products with conditional shelf-life extensions. Distinct from expiry_date; used for stability management.
reference: ICH Q1A(R2) Stability Testing; EU GMP Annex 13; FDA 21 CFR Part 211.137

description: The number of dosage units returned by the subject or site for this kit. Used in drug accountability reconciliation to calculate compliance and account for unused medication.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+; EU GMP Annex 13; FDA 21 CFR Part 312

description: The date and time at which the kit was returned by the subject or site to the depot or destruction facility. Part of the chain-of-custody audit trail for drug accountability.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+; 21 CFR Part 11; EU GMP Annex 13

reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.18; FDA Guidance on Risk-Based Monitoring; EMA Reflection Paper on Risk-Based QM

description: Classification of the deviation by severity and regulatory impact. 'Major' deviations directly affect subject safety, data integrity, or regulatory compliance. 'Minor' deviations have minimal impact.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.5; EMA Guideline on GCP Inspection; FDA Guidance on Protocol Deviations

description: Detailed narrative description of the protocol deviation, including what protocol requirement was not met, the circumstances under which it occurred, and any immediate actions taken. Sourced from the eCRF or CTMS deviation entry.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.5; CDISC SDTM DV Domain (DVTERM); FDA Guidance on Protocol Deviations

description: Externally-known, human-readable unique reference number assigned to the protocol deviation record, typically generated by the CTMS (the source system or EDC (Medidata Rave). Used for cross-system traceability and regulatory correspondence.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.5; 21 CFR Part 312.62; Oracle Siebel CTMS

description: Current workflow lifecycle state of the deviation record. 'Open' indicates newly identified; 'under_review' indicates active investigation; 'resolved' indicates corrective action completed; 'closed' indicates fully adjudicated and archived; 'escalated'
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.5; MasterControl; Oracle Siebel CTMS

description: Functional classification of the deviation describing which protocol requirement was violated. Common types include: eligibility, dosing, visit_window, prohibited_medication, consent, randomization, assessments, sample_collection, concomitant_medication
reference: CDISC SDTM DV Domain; ICH E6(R2); FDA Guidance on Protocol Deviations

description: The date on which the protocol deviation was first identified or discovered, which may differ from the occurrence date. Used to calculate detection lag and assess monitoring effectiveness.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.18; FDA Guidance on Protocol Deviations; Oracle Siebel CTMS

business_glossary_term: Electronic Case Report Form (eCRF) Form Reference
description: Reference to the specific eCRF form or data point in Medidata Rave EDC that is associated with this deviation, enabling direct traceability to the source data record.
reference: CDISC SDTM DV Domain; ICH E6(R2) Section 5.18; Medidata Rave EDC

business_glossary_term: Include in Clinical Study Report (CSR) Flag
description: Indicates whether this deviation must be listed or summarized in the Clinical Study Report (CSR) per ICH E3 requirements. Major and important deviations are typically included.
reference: ICH E3 Section 10.2; ICH E6(R2); FDA Guidance on CSR

description: The date on which the deviation was formally submitted to the IRB/IEC. Used to verify compliance with reporting timelines and to support audit readiness.
reference: 21 CFR Part 56.108; ICH E6(R2) Section 3.3; EU CTR 536/2014

business_glossary_term: Institutional Review Board / Independent Ethics Committee (IRB/IEC) Reporting Required
description: Indicates whether this deviation must be reported to the Institutional Review Board (IRB) or Independent Ethics Committee (IEC) per applicable regulations and the IRB/IEC-approved protocol.
reference: 21 CFR Part 56.108; ICH E6(R2) Section 3.3; EU CTR 536/2014

description: The date on which the protocol deviation actually occurred (i.e., the date the protocol requirement was not met). This is the principal real-world event date per CDISC SDTM DVSTDTC.
reference: CDISC SDTM DV Domain (DVSTDTC); ICH E6(R2); 21 CFR Part 312.62

description: The date on which the Principal Investigator (PI) was formally notified of the deviation. Required for GCP compliance and site management accountability.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.5; 21 CFR Part 312.53; Oracle Siebel CTMS

description: Specific section, clause, or criterion number within the study protocol that was deviated from (e.g., 'Section 5.3 Inclusion Criterion 2'). Enables precise traceability to the protocol document.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 6; CDISC SDTM DV Domain (DVCAT); FDA Guidance on Protocol Deviations

description: Version of the study protocol that was in effect at the time the deviation occurred. Critical for determining which protocol requirements were applicable.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 6; 21 CFR Part 312.23

description: The date on which the deviation was formally submitted to the applicable regulatory authority (FDA, EMA, PMDA, etc.), where regulatory reporting was required.
reference: 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA CT-3 Guidance; ICH E6(R2) Section 5.17; PMDA

description: Indicates whether this deviation must be reported to a regulatory authority (e.g., FDA, EMA, PMDA) as part of IND safety reporting or clinical trial notification obligations.
reference: 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA CT-3 Guidance; ICH E6(R2) Section 5.17

description: Indicates whether this deviation is a recurrence of a previously identified deviation of the same type at the same site or by the same subject. Used for trend analysis and escalation decisions.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.20; FDA Risk-Based Monitoring Guidance; EMA Reflection Paper on QM

description: The date on which the deviation was formally reported to the sponsor, IRB/IEC, or regulatory authority as required. Used to assess compliance with reporting timelines.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.5.2; 21 CFR Part 312.62; EU CTR 536/2014 Article 54

description: The date on which the deviation was resolved and corrective actions were confirmed as complete. Marks the end of the active deviation lifecycle.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.5; MasterControl; Oracle Siebel CTMS

description: Categorized root cause of the deviation as determined during investigation. Common categories include: training_gap, communication_failure, process_gap, system_error, oversight, workload, protocol_complexity, subject_non_compliance.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.20; MasterControl CAPA Module; FDA CAPA Guidance

description: Detailed narrative of the identified root cause of the protocol deviation, as documented during the investigation process. Supports CAPA development and trend analysis.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.20; MasterControl; FDA CAPA Guidance

description: The native record identifier from the originating source system (e.g., Medidata Rave deviation ID or the source system deviation record ID). Enables upstream reconciliation and audit trail.
reference: ALCOA+; 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) Section 5.5

description: The date on which the deviation was formally communicated to the sponsor. Used to verify compliance with sponsor notification timelines per the Clinical Trial Agreement.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.5.2; 21 CFR Part 312.62

description: Indicates whether this deviation must be formally reported to the study sponsor per the Clinical Trial Agreement and sponsor SOPs.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.5.2; 21 CFR Part 312.62

business_glossary_term: Subject Excluded from Per Protocol (PP) Population Flag
description: Indicates whether this deviation resulted in the exclusion of the subject from the Per Protocol (PP) analysis population, as determined by the biostatistics team per the Statistical Analysis Plan (the source system).
reference: ICH E9 Statistical Principles; ICH E9(R1) Estimands; SAP; CDISC ADaM

description: Assessment of whether the deviation had an impact on subject safety, rights, or well-being. Used to determine reporting obligations and CAPA urgency.
reference: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.5; FDA Guidance on Protocol Deviations; EMA GCP Inspection Findings

description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to the protocol deviation record. Supports ALCOA+ audit trail and change tracking requirements.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) Section 8; ALCOA+

description: Unique system-generated identifier for each quality risk assessment record within the compliance domain. Serves as the primary key for the risk_assessment data product.
reference: ICH Q9 Quality Risk Management; FDA Risk-Based Monitoring Guidance

description: Foreign key linking to compliance.audit. Business justification: Risk assessments can be scoped to audits (pre-audit risk assessment, post-audit risk evaluation).

reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Foreign key linking to compliance.compliance_capa. Business justification: Risk assessments with capa_required_flag=true should link to the resulting CAPA. A risk assessment that identifies unacceptable risk triggers a CAPA for remediation.
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Foreign key linking to compliance.compliance_sop. Business justification: Risk assessments are conducted per SOPs and can assess SOP compliance or be governed by a specific SOP.
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Foreign key linking to supply.depot. Business justification: Depot qualification risk assessments evaluate cold chain capability, geographic coverage, and GMP compliance.
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Foreign key to the regulatory inspection associated with this risk assessment.

Foreign key linking to supply.imp_master. Business justification: IMP-specific risk assessments cover stability risks, cold chain requirements, controlled substance handling, and biological product safety.
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Foreign key linking to study.investigational_product. Business justification: IP-specific risk assessments (storage, handling, blinding integrity, controlled substance risk) are a GCP and GMP requirement.
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Foreign key linking to laboratory.lab_facility. Business justification: Risk-based monitoring requires formal risk assessments of laboratory facilities as part of vendor qualification and ongoing oversight.
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Foreign key linking to laboratory.lab_panel. Business justification: Risk assessments are scoped to specific lab panels in clinical operations (e.g., critical safety panels with high risk of missed collections, biomarker panels with complex stability
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Foreign key linking to safety.safety_signal. Business justification: ICH E6 R2 risk-based monitoring requires that identified safety signals directly inform quality risk assessments. Risk management plans are updated when signals are detected.
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Foreign key linking to document.tmf_document. Business justification: Risk assessments reference specific TMF documents as supporting evidence (e.g., protocol, IB, site agreements).
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Date on which the risk assessment was formally approved by the authorized QA signatory. Required for regulatory audit trail and 21 CFR Part 11 electronic records compliance.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2); MasterControl Workflow

description: The date on which the risk assessment was formally conducted and documented. Represents the principal business event date for this record. Used for trend analysis and review frequency tracking.
reference: ICH Q9; ICH E6(R2); FDA RBQM Guidance

description: Current lifecycle state of the risk assessment record in MasterControl: draft (being authored), in_review (under QA/sponsor review), approved (formally accepted), active (monitoring in progress), closed (risk resolved or accepted), cancelled (assessment
reference: MasterControl Workflow; ICH Q9; 21 CFR Part 11

business_glossary_term: Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) Required Flag
description: Indicates whether a formal Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) record must be initiated as a result of this risk assessment. Typically set to True when residual risk rating is critical or high, or when identified gaps meet CAPA threshold criteria.
reference: ICH Q9; ICH E6(R2); FDA 21 CFR Part 820; MasterControl CAPA Module

description: Narrative description of the existing or planned quality control and risk mitigation measures applied to reduce the identified risk (e.g., enhanced SDV, targeted monitoring, additional training, SOP updates, EDC edit checks). Sourced from MasterControl.
reference: ICH Q9; ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA RBQM Guidance

description: Timestamp when this risk assessment record was first created in the source system (MasterControl). Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and ICH E6(R2) for electronic records.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2); GDPR Article 5

description: Indicates whether the identified risk has a potential or actual impact on clinical data integrity (ALCOA+ principles: Attributable, Legible, Contemporaneous, Original, Accurate). Triggers enhanced data review and potential database lock delay.
reference: FDA Data Integrity Guidance; ALCOA+; ICH E6(R2); MHRA GXP Data Integrity Guidance

description: Indicates whether the identified risk has a direct impact on Good Clinical Practice (GCP) compliance. Drives escalation to QA leadership and potential regulatory notification obligations.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; EMA GCP Guideline

description: Narrative description of quality gaps, process deficiencies, or compliance vulnerabilities identified during the risk assessment (e.g., missing SDV documentation, incomplete ICF versions, delayed SAE reporting).
reference: ICH Q9; ICH E6(R2); FDA RBQM Guidance; EMA GCP Guideline

description: Numeric score (typically 1–5) representing the ability to detect the risk before it causes harm, prior to control measures. Used in FMEA-style risk scoring (Risk Priority Number = Likelihood × Impact × Detectability).
reference: ICH Q9 FMEA Methodology; FDA RBQM Guidance

description: Numeric score (typically 1–5) representing the severity of impact on patient safety, data integrity, or regulatory compliance if the risk materializes before controls are applied. Component of the inherent risk score calculation.
reference: ICH Q9; FDA RBQM Guidance; ICH E6(R2)

description: Numeric score (typically 1–5) representing the probability of the risk occurring before any control measures are applied. Component of the inherent risk score calculation per ICH Q9 risk estimation methodology.
reference: ICH Q9; FDA RBQM Guidance

description: Qualitative risk rating derived from the inherent risk score before controls: critical, high, medium, or low. Used for risk prioritization, escalation thresholds, and sponsor/QA reporting dashboards.
reference: ICH Q9; FDA RBQM Guidance; EMA GCP Guideline

description: Composite numeric risk score calculated before control measures are applied, typically derived from likelihood, impact, and detectability scores (e.g., product or weighted sum). Establishes the baseline risk level for prioritization.
reference: ICH Q9; FDA RBQM Guidance; EMA Reflection Paper on RBQM

description: Indicates whether this risk assessment was conducted specifically in preparation for a regulatory inspection (FDA, EMA, MHRA, PMDA, or sponsor audit). Enables filtering of inspection-readiness assessments for pre-inspection reporting.
reference: FDA Inspection Guidance; EMA GCP Inspection Procedure; ICH E6(R2)

description: The native record identifier assigned by MasterControl (the system of record for this data product) to the risk assessment document. Enables direct traceability back to the source system for audit and reconciliation purposes.
reference: MasterControl Document Control; 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2)

description: Scheduled date for the next periodic review of this risk assessment, based on the defined review frequency. Supports proactive risk monitoring and inspection readiness. Calculated from assessment_date and review_frequency_days.
reference: ICH Q9; FDA RBQM Guidance; EMA Reflection Paper on RBQM

description: Externally-known, human-readable unique reference number assigned to the risk assessment record in MasterControl (e.g., RA-2024-00123). Used for cross-system traceability, audit trails, and regulatory inspection readiness.
reference: MasterControl Document Control; ICH Q9; 21 CFR Part 11

description: The primary regulatory authority whose standards and guidelines govern this risk assessment (e.g., FDA, EMA, MHRA, PMDA, TGA, Health Canada). Determines applicable GCP framework and reporting obligations.
reference: FDA 21 CFR Part 312; EMA GCP Guideline; ICH E6(R2); MHRA GCP Guidance

description: Documented plan for addressing identified gaps and reducing residual risk, including specific actions, responsible parties, and target timelines. Distinct from CAPA (which is a formal corrective/preventive action record); this is the risk-level
reference: ICH Q9; FDA RBQM Guidance; ICH E6(R2)

description: Current status of remediation activities for identified gaps: not_started, in_progress, completed, or overdue. Supports inspection readiness dashboards and QA oversight reporting.
reference: ICH Q9; FDA RBQM Guidance; MasterControl Workflow

description: Target completion date for the remediation actions identified in the risk assessment. Used for tracking remediation progress and escalation when overdue.
reference: ICH Q9; FDA RBQM Guidance; MasterControl CAPA Tracking

description: Numeric score (typically 1–5) representing the ability to detect the risk after control measures are in place. Component of the residual risk score calculation.
reference: ICH Q9 FMEA Methodology; FDA RBQM Guidance

description: Numeric score (typically 1–5) representing the severity of impact after control measures have been applied. Used to calculate the residual risk score.
reference: ICH Q9; FDA RBQM Guidance

description: Numeric score (typically 1–5) representing the probability of the risk occurring after control measures have been applied. Used to calculate the residual risk score.
reference: ICH Q9; FDA RBQM Guidance

description: Qualitative risk rating after control measures are applied: critical, high, medium, or low. Drives risk acceptance decisions, escalation to DSMB/DMC, and CAPA initiation. A residual rating of critical or high typically triggers mandatory CAPA.
reference: ICH Q9; FDA RBQM Guidance; ICH E6(R2)

description: Composite numeric risk score calculated after control measures are applied. Represents the remaining risk exposure. Compared against risk acceptance thresholds to determine if further mitigation is required.
reference: ICH Q9; FDA RBQM Guidance; EMA Reflection Paper on RBQM

description: Defined interval in calendar days between periodic re-assessments of this risk (e.g., 30, 60, 90, 180 days). Drives scheduling of next_review_date and ensures ongoing risk monitoring per ICH Q9 principles.
reference: ICH Q9; FDA RBQM Guidance

description: Formal decision on whether the residual risk level is acceptable: accepted (risk within tolerance), not_accepted (requires further mitigation or CAPA), or conditionally_accepted (accepted with defined monitoring conditions).
reference: ICH Q9; FDA RBQM Guidance; EMA GCP Guideline

description: High-level classification of the risk domain being assessed: data_integrity (ALCOA+ violations, EDC issues), patient_safety (adverse event under-reporting, protocol deviations), regulatory_compliance (GCP, ICH, FDA/EMA non-compliance), or operational
reference: ICH Q9; ICH E6(R2); FDA 21 CFR Part 312; EMA GCP Guideline

description: Detailed narrative describing the identified risk, including the potential failure mode, root cause hypothesis, and potential impact on study quality, patient safety, or regulatory compliance. Sourced from MasterControl risk assessment form.
reference: ICH Q9; ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA RBQM Guidance

description: Organizational department of the risk owner (e.g., Quality Assurance, Data Management, Clinical Operations, Regulatory Affairs). Used for departmental risk reporting and workload analysis.
reference: ICH Q9; MasterControl Workflow

description: More granular classification within the risk category (e.g., 'Source Data Verification', 'Informed Consent Process', 'SAE Reporting Timeliness', 'Protocol Deviation Management'). Enables detailed risk trending and root cause analysis.
reference: ICH Q9; CDISC RBQM Framework; FDA RBQM Guidance

description: Defines the level at which the risk assessment was conducted: study-level (entire protocol), site-level (specific investigational site), process-level (e.g., data management, consent), system-level (e.g., EDC, CTMS), or inspection-readiness
reference: ICH Q9; FDA RBQM Guidance; EMA Reflection Paper on Risk-Based Quality Management

description: Indicates whether the study sponsor has been formally notified of this risk assessment and its findings, as required by the Clinical Trial Agreement and GCP obligations. Relevant for high/critical risk ratings.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; EMA GCP Guideline

description: Indicates whether the identified risk has a potential or actual impact on the safety of study subjects/patients. Triggers mandatory escalation to the Principal Investigator (PI), DSMB/DMC, and sponsor safety team.
reference: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; ICH E2A; Declaration of Helsinki

description: Descriptive title summarizing the subject and scope of the risk assessment (e.g., 'Site-Level GCP Compliance Risk Assessment – Site 1042 Q3 2024'). Used for identification and reporting.
reference: ICH Q9; FDA RBQM Guidance

description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to this risk assessment record in the source system. Required for change tracking, audit trail compliance, and Silver layer incremental load processing.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2); GDPR Article 5

description: Unique surrogate identifier for each electronic signature record applied to a controlled document. Primary key for the document_signature data product in the Databricks Silver Layer.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP

description: Reference to the delegation of authority record when the signer is acting on behalf of another party (e.g., a sub-investigator signing on behalf of the Principal Investigator). Supports sponsor oversight and GCP compliance verification.
reference: ICH E6(R2) §4.2; 21 CFR Part 312.62

description: Reference to the clinical study (protocol) with which the signed document is associated. Enables study-level signature completeness reporting and TMF inspection readiness tracking.
reference: ICH E6(R2) §8; DIA TMF Reference Model Zone/Section/Artifact taxonomy

description: Reference to the investigational site associated with the signed document, where applicable (e.g., site-level ICF, site initiation documents). Supports site-level TMF completeness and inspection readiness metrics.
reference: ICH E6(R2) §8.3; DIA TMF Reference Model

description: Reference to the controlled document record in the document master that this signature was applied to. Links the signature to its parent TMF/eTMF document.
reference: DIA TMF Reference Model; Veeva Vault Document Object

description: Reference to the specific version of the document at the time the signature was applied. Ensures the signature is bound to an immutable document version, satisfying 21 CFR Part 11 integrity requirements.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11 §11.10(e); ICH E6(R2) §8

description: Foreign key linking to document.document_workflow. Business justification: Electronic signatures are applied within the context of a document workflow step (review, approval, distribution).
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Cryptographic hash (e.g., SHA-256) of the signed document content and signature metadata at the time of signing. Provides tamper-evidence and integrity verification for the electronic signature record, satisfying 21 CFR Part 11 §11.10(a) data integrity
reference: 21 CFR Part 11 §11.10(a); NIST SP 800-57; FDA Guidance on Electronic Records

description: Free-text comments or notes entered by the signer at the time of signing. May capture the signer's attestation statement, conditional approval notes, or reviewer observations. Stored as part of the immutable signature audit trail.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11 §11.50; Veeva Vault eSignature Module

description: System-generated timestamp when the signature request record was first created in the source system (Veeva Vault). Supports audit trail completeness and ALCOA+ compliance.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11 §11.10(e); ALCOA+

description: Unique identifier of the device (workstation, tablet, or mobile device) used to apply the electronic signature. Supports forensic audit trail and 21 CFR Part 11 system access controls validation.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11 §11.10(d); FDA Guidance on Electronic Records

description: Serial number of the digital certificate used when the signature method is digital_certificate or smart_card. Enables certificate chain validation and revocation checking for PKI-based electronic signatures.

description: The deadline by which the signer must apply their electronic signature, as defined in the document workflow configuration. Used for SLA tracking, escalation triggering, and inspection readiness reporting.

description: Cryptographic algorithm used to generate the audit hash for this signature record (e.g., SHA-256, SHA-512). Required to enable future hash verification and to document the cryptographic standard applied at the time of signing.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11 §11.10(a); NIST FIPS 180-4

description: Indicates whether this signature record has been reviewed and confirmed as complete and compliant for regulatory inspection purposes. Used in TMF inspection readiness dashboards and GCP audit preparation.
reference: ICH E6(R2) §8; DIA TMF Reference Model; FDA GCP Inspection Guidance

description: IP address of the device from which the electronic signature was applied. Captured as part of the 21 CFR Part 11 audit trail to support identity verification and forensic investigation. May be considered PII under GDPR.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11 §11.10(e); GDPR Article 4(1); EU CTR 536/2014

description: Indicates whether this signature is part of a document package intended for regulatory submission (e.g., IND, NDA, BLA, MAA, eCTD). When True, the signature record is subject to heightened integrity and retention requirements.
reference: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH M4 CTD; FDA eCTD Guidance; EMA eCTD Guidance

description: Date and time of the most recent automated reminder notification sent to the signer. Supports escalation management and overdue signature tracking.
reference: Veeva Vault eSignature Workflow; DIA TMF Reference Model

description: IETF BCP 47 locale code representing the language and regional settings active at the time of signing (e.g., en-US, de-DE, ja-JP). Relevant for multi-national trials to confirm the signer viewed the document in their preferred language.
